News.title: Multiple deaths after police vehicle and car crash during pursuit
News.content:
Multiple people have died in a crash involving a police vehicle and a car following a pursuit, police have said.

The collision involved a police vehicle and a Volkswagen Passat on the A66 in South Bank, near Middlesbrough in Teesside, at about 03:39 BST, Cleveland Police said.

North East Ambulance Service said 14 "ambulance resources" attended and "a number of patients died at the scene".

A police spokesman said: "Sadly, the collision has resulted in multiple fatalities. We are working to identify the victims and contact their families."

The Independent Office for Police Conduct said it was opening an investigation.

The watchdog said: "At this early stage, we understand Cleveland Police sighted a suspicious vehicle and a pursuit began."

News.title: How this 1960s ex-council house is managing to stay cool without air con
News.content:
After five heatwaves and plenty of advice on how to stay safe in what is set to become the UK's hottest summer on record, many people continue to find it a challenge to stay cool - particularly in their homes.

This is perhaps no surprise. More than half of homes, external in the UK are already at risk of overheating and at current rates of climate change this will rise to 92% by 2050 if we do not adapt.

But in south London, on a 35C day, one 1960s ex-council house with no air-conditioning is managing to beat the heat.

Marion Baeli's home is one of many across the UK being adapted for warmer - maybe even 40C - British summers.

News.title: GTA 6 leaks - a nightmare or a blip for the biggest video game of the year?
News.content:
Video game journalist Wesley Yin-Poole, director of news at IGN, says the apparent leaks will be tough for the game's developers.

"GTA 6 is an enormous endeavour," says Yin-Poole. "It's being built over the course a decade, essentially, with thousands of people involved.

"To have the game exposed in this way will have been devastating to many people who worked on it."

The group behind the apparent leaks claims to be acting in the interests of players, accusing Rockstar of engaging in anti-consumer practices, such as its decision not to release a disc version of GTA 6 at launch.

Not everyone is convinced about the group's intentions, as each release of new material has invited viewers to send cryptocurrency "donations" to the user uploading them.

Stop Killing Games, which campaigns against all-digital distribution models, criticised the alleged leaks as "destructive" and urged people not to send money to those claiming responsibility.

Yin-Poole says there's "a huge amount of scepticism" about the stated motivation.

"Most people believe this is about money," he says, "it feels like, honestly, the whole 'we're doing this for the gamers' angle is nonsense, and I suspect most people have dismissed it."

So far, two official trailers for GTA 6 have been released, the most recent in May 2025. Since then, ardent fans have leapt on any rumours or apparent clues in official Rockstar posts.

Some famously came up with an elaborate theory, external suggesting an image of the moon included in a promotional post for GTA Online held clues to the release date of GTA 6's first trailer.

"To a certain extent, Rockstar has themselves to blame," says Vermeij. "That's their strategy - and I think it's a good strategy, it's exciting. But the consequence is that every little bit of information, every little event, gets sort of blown out of proportion."

Yin-Poole says while people will likely understand this isn't the way Rockstar had intended GTA6 to be revealed and doesn't show the game in the best light, he believes most will "reserve judgement" about it until they have seen official footage in action, or played it for themselves.

Ultimately, he believes there's little chance the leaks will "derail the potential success of the game".

"GTA 6 will be an unprecedented moment in pop culture history," he says. "So ultimately, this will become a footnote in the history of GTA 6's development."

Vermeij, who has not watched any of the latest leaks, agrees.

"I think it will have no impact at all whatsoever," he says. "People will have forgotten about it by the time the game comes out."

Grand Theft Auto 6 is due to be released on 19 November for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S, with a PC release expected at a later date.

News.title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs
News.content:
More new students are choosing to live at home for university this year than in the last nine years, new data shows.

Over 81,000 UK 18-year-olds said in their accepted university application that they intended to live at home this year, according to the Universities and Colleges Admissions Service (Ucas) - just over one in three students in that category.

In 2017, it was closer to one in five.

The figures vary across the UK - with 48% of applicants in Scotland intending to live at home, compared with 20% in Wales - but the trend is rising across the board.

Students told the BBC the rising cost of living was a major influence in deciding what to do after school or college.

For friends Beatrice and Amelia, who are from St Helens, Merseyside, the cost of accommodation was a big factor in their decision to live at home while studying.

Both are heading to university in September, but neither will be moving into student accommodation.

News.title: As they return to the UK, Harry and Meghan search for a brand that sticks
News.content:
In late July, the Duchess of Sussex's lifestyle range, called As ever, launched a "rich, vibrant" blackberry spread alongside a softly lit video of her picking the fruit.

A month later, Meghan and her husband Prince Harry are returning to live in the UK just as blackberry season ends. Perhaps we can expect another video soon, shot on these shores.

Or perhaps not, because experts say the Harry and Meghan brand is at a crossroads.

After the Duke and Duchess of Sussex's acrimonious exit from the Royal Family in 2020, the projects marking their fresh start in California - from streaming to signature scents - have mostly failed to find large audiences, and experts say it's unclear where the couple goes from here.

Their return to the UK has surprised many and we don't know their reasons for the switch, but what's clear is that they will not be working royals when they return. So what could they be doing instead?

News.title: Drugs at their fingertips, intense pressure: Why child stars fall into addiction
News.content:
Hayden Panettiere was 16 when drugs first arrived in her life in Hollywood.

Ahead of a red carpet event for the hit series Heroes, she has said someone on her team handed her a pill to help amp up her energy. The hit sci-fi NBC series had catapulted the teen into a household name - and that brought with it intense pressure and exhaustion she says felt overwhelming.

"Within minutes, a wave of energy washed over me, like I'd just woken up from the most refreshing night's sleep of my life," Panettiere wrote about that pill in her memoir, which was released just months before her death.

She called it "the gateway drug that ushered me toward the good of pharmaceuticals and the downfall of addiction".

The star's sudden death at the age of 36 has placed a renewed focus on her struggles with mental health and substance abuse, and re-ignited a discussion about the pressures of Hollywood on child stars.

The coroner's office in Greenville, South Carolina said crews treated a woman in "cardiac arrest" and her autopsy showed "no signs of trauma".

No cause of death has been released, though additional tests are yet to be completed.

Audio from police dispatchers and crews who responded to the address said they were responding to a "cardiac arrest" and detailed their efforts to resuscitate the woman after a possible "overdose". Panettiere's ex boyfriend, Brian Hickerson - who has admitted to abusing her - and his brother Zack, were with Panettiere when emergency services came, according to a police report.

There is no suggestion of wrongdoing on their part, according to police.

It is not known if drugs or alcohol played a factor in her death, but the US Drug Enforcement Agency is joining an investigation into her death, according to US media reports.

Panettiere is one of many actors who has openly struggled with addiction after exposure to fame at an early age, which addiction experts told the BBC can put people at risk for mental health and substance abuse issues.

It can sometimes seem to the rest of the world that child actors have "everything" at their fingertips - like fame and money, said Lucas Trautman, the medical director of Oxford Treatment Center, an addiction treatment centre in Mississippi.

"But it's important to remember that they were also exposed during a developmental time to many adult aspects of life that the rest of us weren't - including traumatic experiences - and so that gives them unique risk factors for addiction," Trautman said.

Panettiere's death comes after she published a memoir where she discussed at length her issues with addiction, her postpartum depression and the loss of her 28-year-old brother.

Panettiere's decision to publicly share her struggles is worthy of respect, said William Moyers, the vice-president of public affairs for Hazelden Betty Ford, the largest nonprofit addiction treatment provider in the US. But he said the constant public scrutiny she faced may not have allowed her room to address her mental health in private.

"Her entire life from the beginning was centred in the intense public spotlight, and this didn't give Hayden much in the way of a respite," said Moyers, who has been in recovery from an addiction since 1989.

News.title: These bookshops let Chinese readers question their country, now the doors are closing
News.content:
When Chen Zhu heads to Hong Kong from mainland China every month, there's one place she always goes: Hunter Bookstore.

Founded four years ago by a former councillor, the independent bookshop has earned a reputation for stocking what authorities would consider sensitive books - accounts of Hong Kong's pro-democracy campaigners to famous allegories on authoritarianism, such as George Orwell's Animal Farm or Hajime Isayama's Manga series Attack on Titan.

It's a short journey from Zhu's home in Guangzhou on China's southern coast to the crowded street in Hong Kong's Sham Shui Po district, where Hunter is sandwiched between fabric sellers, garages and trendy cafes.

But, for the 23-year-old, it is also a passage into a different, freer world - where she can find answers to forbidden questions.

When she learned the bookshop had been raided by police in late June, Zhu broke into tears: "I was devastated."

Hong Kong saw a boom in independent bookshops after huge pro-democracy protests rocked the city in 2019. But it has been increasingly difficult for them to survive as China's control over the city has grown.

While Beijing defends its far-reaching National Security Law (NSL) as essential for stability, many Hong Kongers and rights groups argue it has crushed free speech. Thousands of locals, including activists and former lawmakers, have left in recent years, as tough new security laws have led to a slew of arrests and convictions.

News.title: Girl, 6, dies days after Shoreham sea tragedy killed three family members
News.content:
A six-year-old girl has died in hospital after getting into difficulty in the sea off Shoreham in West Sussex, in an incident which also killed her father, mother and sister.

Saja El-Khawas, a British Palestinian from London, was pulled from the sea by emergency crews on Tuesday.

Her father Hassan El-Khawas, 55, mother Zeina Alayn, 37, and 14-year-old sister Sara, died despite the efforts of paramedics at the scene.

Emergency services were called to the sea off Shoreham Fort at about 14:40 BST on Tuesday to a report of four people in difficulty in the water.

News.title: Advisor O'Neill rules out government job but backs PM's devolution plans
News.content:
The economist Lord Jim O'Neill, who has been advising the prime minister, has said he will not be taking a job in Andy Burnham's government.

Lord O'Neill, a crossbench peer, was once a treasury minister under the Conservatives.

As first reported by, external the Financial Times, he said he did not want the constraints involved in taking on a formal role.

The former chief economist at Goldman Sachs had been tipped to become Burnham's chief economic adviser.

He said he was enjoying what he was currently doing too much and did not want to have to give up control of his business interests to comply with official rules.

He told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that he had "lots of other things that are going on that I very much enjoy" and, having been a minister before, he knew the job included "all the constraints that understandably go with it, like a blind trust and to abandon everything else you do, never mind the fact that it's 24/7".

In placing shares in blind trusts, ministers have no knowledge of how their investment is being handled, to avoid any potential conflict of interest.

He said he concluded he would rather be a voice to talk to and "get on with the rest of the things in my life".

He earlier told the Financial Times it was "not because of any policy disagreements", adding "I'm a massive fan of the focus on devolution and I hope Andy and his team will be bold on this and everything else."

He pointed to Greater Manchester as an example of economic growth and said if you could repeat that around populated areas, "then national economic performance will improve".

Asked by the BBC whether the new government in the upcoming October budget would need to raise taxes, Lord O'Neill said it was a choice for the prime minister and his team "based on the things they're saying they want to do more of - defence spending is obviously the one that catches the eye", among other things.

Pressed on whether the government could turn to something such as wealth taxes, Lord O'Neill said he was "not a fan of further increases in these kind of taxes, particularly as it relates to capital gains for genuine risk taking things like venture capital".

He noted that the country has boosted government spending "dramatically" in recent years and needed a "more sensible approach to welfare spending under genuine welfare reform".

From 2015-2016, Lord O'Neill was commercial secretary to the Treasury under the then-Chancellor, George Osborne.

The peer, who grew up in Greater Manchester, was a key figure in pushing the Conservatives' Northern Powerhouse agenda, which was aimed at boosting the economy of the North of England.

Lord O'Neill is also known as the economist who coined the term Bric in 2001 to describe leading developing or newly industrialised countries with potential for fast growth and, therefore, investment returns.

The original four nations - Brazil, Russia, India and China - later became the Brics when they were joined by South Africa.

News.title: Brief break from rain as sunshine returns for weekend
News.content:
After the spell of showery weather earlier this week, a strong area of high pressure is set to bring bright and sunny weather to much of the UK this weekend.

Daytime temperatures will feel pleasantly warm - though a long way off from the record heat experienced earlier this month.

Nights are expected to be mostly clear, leading to a significant temperature contrast from morning lows to afternoon highs.

While Saturday and Sunday will bring a brief break from the rain for many, unsettled weather will return early next week.

News.title: Meghan in talks for role in Netflix series The Gentlemen, BBC understands
News.content:
The Duchess of Sussex is in talks to return to acting with a role in Netflix series The Gentlemen, the BBC has learned.

Discussions are in their early stages but this would be Meghan's first significant acting role since her marriage to Prince Harry.

Much of the two previous series of The Gentlemen, which was created by Guy Ritchie, have been filmed in the Cotswolds - the area it is rumoured Harry and Meghan will set up home when they return to the UK later this month.

The Gentlemen, starring the actor Theo James, is a comedy series about a duke who becomes a drug baron.

The details of the discussions and any role Meghan might be offered have not yet been revealed.

Actors Hugh Bonneville and Vinnie Jones have appeared in previous series of the show.

Meghan was best known in acting for her part in the US legal drama, Suits, in which she played lawyer, Rachel Zane, for seven seasons. Her last episode aired in 2018.

News.title: Murder probe after wildfire uncovers body in park
News.content:
A murder investigation is under way after human bones were uncovered at a west London park following a wildfire, the Metropolitan Police said.

Emergency services were called to Bedfont Pits in Hounslow at about 18:35 BST on Wednesday, 12 August.

A police spokesperson said the remains were found by a member of the public after the wildfire affected an area of woodland known as The Pits.

Following a post-mortem examination, police said the bones belonged to a woman aged between 25 and 45. They said it was not clear how long the remains had been there and officers were still working to identify her.

News.title: Arran ferry evacuated over 'bomb threat' by passenger rescued from sea
News.content:
A 23-year-old man has been arrested after a ferry service on Scotland's west coast was evacuated over a bomb threat.

Operator CalMac said a passenger was reported overboard on the MV Caledonian Isles 16:40 service, carrying 329 people from Brodick on the Isle of Arran.

The BBC understands that after being pulled from the sea by the ferry's rescue boat, the man then told crew that there was a bomb on board.

All passengers were removed on foot at Ardrossan so the vessel could be searched. Police Scotland said it was established that the threats "were not credible".

The passengers and others waiting at the port were taken to a nearby supermarket car park by police while the search was carried out.

After this was complete, officers allowed people back on board to collect their vehicles.

News.title: Teen blinded by firework wants ban on public sales
News.content:
A teenager blinded by a firework on Bonfire Night has called for a ban on them being sold to the public.

Tom Parnaby was 18 when he and a friend were badly injured in the accident on 5 November 2025.

He is now campaigning for more controlled firework displays and tighter regulations on sales.

Tom, who has since become a father for the first time, said despite what happened to him he does not hate fireworks, but thinks the "public sale of them is crazy".

Tom suffered injuries to his face leading to him losing his sight during an incident with friends on the beach in Scarborough, North Yorkshire.

The teenager said focusing on the baby daughter who he would never be able to see had helped him pull through.

"I am just grateful to have her with me," he said.

"It is a lot easier to focus on what's coming than what's behind with her there."

News.title: Man tracks down siblings who sent him Christmas present as he fled war 33 years ago
News.content:
A man forced to flee war in Croatia as a child has used social media to find and thank the siblings from Wales, who sent him a Christmas present more than 30 years ago.

Dalibor Sentic was 10 when in the early 1990s his family fled the newly independent country - which had recently become involved in the Balkan war - for Stockholm, Sweden.

Dalibor had received a gift from two young siblings, eight-year-old Claire and Peter, six, from Mold, Flintshire, and had hoped to track them down but only had limited information on them.

Decades later, Dalibor, now 44, was able to find the pair to thank them, saying the gesture had "meant a lot" at a time of great difficulty.

Describing fleeing his homeland as a child, Dalibor said "we had basically nothing".

"It was like starting all over again.

"I was so innocent but remember hearing the bombs," he said.

Dalibor said that, despite the conflict surrounding them, his parents made sure he felt "loved and secure", although he added that moving countries was "tough on a kid".

Some months before they fled, Dalibor said his teacher took him into a room full of packages, telling him to choose one to open.

It contained a picture of Claire and Peter, which he held onto for more than three decades.

"The older you get the more you understand the meaning behind small gestures... it meant a lot," he said.

News.title: Prince Harry and six others face privacy case legal bill of up to £34.5m
News.content:
Prince Harry and six other public figures face paying up to Â£34.5m to the publisher of the Daily Mail after a High Court judge imposed an exceptional order for legal costs over their failed privacy case.

The seven claimants, also including Sir Elton John and Liz Hurley, must pay an initial Â£9.54m by Friday of next week to Associated Newspapers Limited (ANL).

The judge ruled that the case was a rare one in which the claimants should have to pay far in excess of the costs that had been agreed before trial, criticising how they presented their claims as "unreasonable to a high degree".

On 7 July, Judge Mr Justice Nicklin dismissed the claims of unlawful information-gathering, which ANL denied.

The Duke of Sussex and the other six claimants have until 2 October to attempt to launch an appeal.

Those other claimants are Sir Elton John and his husband David Furnish, former Liberal Democrat deputy leader Sir Simon Hughes, racial justice campaigner Baroness Lawrence, and actresses Sadie Frost and Liz Hurley,

They had insurance to cover up to Â£16.2m of Association Newspapers' costs in the event of losing the case - but Friday's ruling means the newspaper group could now try to recover up to the Â£34.5m that it said it had to spend to defend itself. This means the duke and others could face a bill of some Â£18m.

Justice Nicklin said: "I regard a claim for costs in excess of Â£34 million as, on its face, excessive and as giving rise to real concerns as to whether all of the costs now claimed by Associated were reasonably incurred and are reasonable in amount."

But he added he had "decided not to impose a ceiling on Associated's recoverable costs", as it would "be too broad-brushed, would risk unfairness, and would be vulnerable to the charge that it was arbitrary".

The judge also ruled that ANL's costs should be determined on an indemnity basis, which is more favourable to the publisher in terms of the amount it can recover, aside from where orders had already been made.

He added it was "striking" that "not a single allegation of serious wrongdoing was voluntarily withdrawn" by the group of seven claimants.

He said: "That matters. Serious allegations of criminality or grave impropriety cannot properly be left hanging over individuals in that way.

"If a party no longer advances such an allegation, or no longer has a proper evidential basis for advancing it, the allegation should be withdrawn clearly and in terms.

Vivian Campbell, the guitarist for Def Leppard, has revealed that he is undergoing treatment for cancer again following an unsuccessful donor transplant.

The rock musician, 63, first revealed in 2013 that he had been diagnosed with Hodgkin’s lymphoma, which then returned in 2015 before more treatment.

During an interview with El Salvadorian radio station YSKL, Campbell said: ““There’s only been one time that I felt it was gonna kill me. In the winter of 2023, I got really scared about what was happening and the pace at which it was happening.

“And I realised at that point that I had to do a donor transplant. It was my only hope to survive.”

open image in gallery Vivian Campbell at the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 2025 ( Getty Images )

Campbell revealed that he got a stem cell transplant in January 2025, but it “didn’t stick”.

“So the cancer has returned, and I’m continuing treatments to manage it,” he explained.

The guitarist said that he hopes to undergo another transplant operation within a few years, and intends to keep performing with Def Leppard as the heavy metal band continue to release new music and tour.

Campbell told the interviewer that he tries to keep “moving forward” and preoccupy himself with projects.

“I do think that that’s what helped me, even when I was at a really low ebb with cancer treatment,” he said. “The fact that I could still continue to work, that gives me something to live for. Something that you enjoy, that you’re passionate about, that you can wake up in the morning and look forward to.

“I think that deflects, that takes away from focusing too much on cancer.”

Campbell joined Def Leppard in 1992, following the death by overdose of previous guitarist Steve Clark in 1991.

Formed in Sheffield in 1977 by singer Joe Elliott, bassist Rick Savage, guitarist Pete Willis, and drummer Tony Kenning, Def Leppard went on to become one of the most popular music artists of all time.

The band are currently midway through an international tour, having recently performed in stadia around the UK.

Their next tour dates are in the US , before travelling to Mexico and Central and South America in October and November.

George Russell delivered a much-needed boost to his championship hopes with a commanding victory in the Dutch Grand Prix sprint.

Russell endured a tough run at the last three races but has returned from the sport’s summer shutdown determined to trust his instincts in order to chase down championship leader and Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli.

The 28-year-old shaved three points off Antonelli’s lead to sit 56 back ahead of Sunday’s main race.

The Italian, who turns 20 next week, crossed the line in fourth in Saturday’s 24-lap dash around the seaside circuit of Zandvoort – hosting the final Dutch Grand Prix before it drops off the calendar.

open image in gallery Kimi Antonelli extended his championship lead (David Davies/PA) ( PA Wire )

That meant he actually extended his lead at the top of the standings by three points to 53, with second-placed Lewis Hamilton trudging home in seventh in a disappointing display as he bids to ignite his charge towards an eighth world title over the second half of the season.

Lando Norris, who earned his first win of the season in Budapest last time out, started second but was unable to offer a significant threat to Russell.

He instead fell back in the closing stages, losing out to Charles Leclerc on lap 17.

Oscar Piastri was fifth in the second McLaren and Max Verstappen, fresh from signing his new Red Bull contract, finished sixth.

open image in gallery Lewis Hamilton struggled in the Dutch Grand Prix sprint (David Davies/PA) ( PA Wire )

Russell produced a confident drive to clinch his third sprint win of the season, blasting away from pole to fend off the threat of Norris before pulling clear.

Ferrari rolled the dice with Leclerc, starting him on soft tyres from third on the grid but it was a move which did not immediately pay off as he was unable to make progress at the start.

Behind him, Antonelli got the jump on Piastri around the outside of the opening corner to claim fourth.

It was a sprint that will not live long in the memory, with that move the only one of note throughout the first 17 laps.

That was until Leclerc closed within striking distance of Norris and dived up the inside of turn one to pass the reigning world champion.

Norris was then under pressure from Antonelli, the Italian on his gearbox through turn one on the final lap, but the British driver held on to claim the third spot on the sprint podium.

Russell took the chequered flag 1.3 seconds ahead of Leclerc.

As he celebrated trackside, the heavens opened and Russell admitted he was grateful for the timing of the weather.

open image in gallery Russell never looked under threat during the sprint (David Davies/PA) ( PA Wire )

“Great start to the weekend, one more lap (and) it would have been a very different end to the race, so I’m glad the rain came when it did!” he said.

“It is going to be a tight one this afternoon (qualifying), Ferrari looked very fast.

“I knew if there was going to be overtakes, it would be towards the end of the race. I knew I wanted to manage my tyres through the high-speed corners and have more in the tank come the end of the race.”

Qualifying for Sunday’s main event gets under way at 4pm local time (3pm BST).

Manchester United begin their 2026/27 Premier League campaign with a trip across the country to take on Hull City. Michael Carrick starts his first full season as manager having impressed during his interim tenure last season.

A mixed pre-season campaign has seen the squad come through it relatively unscathed with only Mason Mount suffering a significant injury which is likely to keep him on the sidelines. United have also replaced Casemiro with midfield reinforcements Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans while they are negotiating to bring in Brighton’s Carlos Baleba as well.

The Red Devils’ opponents are Hull City who won promotion from the Championship via the play-offs. Hull finished 6th in the second division with 21 wins from their 46 games but only won one of their last seven league matches before victory in play-off rounds against Millwall and Middlesbrough in the final.

Their aim for the season is to secure their place in the top-flight and any points they can take of United in this opening encounter will be beneficial for the rest of their season. Here’s everything you need to know:

When is Hull vs Manchester United?

Hull host Manchester United on Saturday 22 August at the MKM Stadium with kick off at 12.30pm, making it the second fixture of the top-flight season after Arsenal take on Coventry on Friday evening.

How can I watch it?

The match will be broadcast on TNT Sports 1 and TNT Sports Ultimate with coverage beginning at 11am. The game will also be streamed live on Discovery+, though it will require an active subscription to watch.

What is the teams news?

Hull City have plenty of injuries to navigate with key players missing. Goalkeeper Jack Butland is out and so to are defenders John Egan, Cody Drameh, Charlie Hughes, and Jens Hjertø-Dahl. In midfield Darko Gyabi, Paddy McNair, Matty Jacob, and Oscar Zambrano are absent while forwards Liam Millar and Enis Destan are unlikely to feature.

Michael Carrick, meanwhile, has a fair amount of squad players to select from. Benjamin Sesko is back in training despite not taking part in pre-season though he could make an appearance off the bench. Matthijs de Ligt has also trained but his recovery will be managed and he is not expected to return until October. Mason Mount meanwhile has a foot issue, sustained in the draw with PSG and will not play. Manuel Ugarte is a long-term absentee due to an ACL injury picked up in the World Cup.

News.title: Mahatma Gandhi’s 688 handwritten messages to grieving friend sell for record £1.2m
News.content:

A collection of 688 handwritten reflections by Mahatma Gandhi has sold for £1.2m at an auction in India, setting a record for an Indian historical document sold at auction.

The handwritten messages were addressed to Anand T Hingorani, a close associate of Gandhi and a fellow participant in India’s independence movement.

They were written over almost two years, from 20 November 1944 to 10 October 1946, and were later compiled into a book called A Thought for the Day, according to auction house Saffronart.

The circumstances in which they were written were deeply personal; Hingorani’s wife Vidya had died, and he shared his loneliness and grief with Gandhi while undergoing nature-cure treatment for deafness, according to the Hingorani family.

Gandhi responded by writing him a thought each day, turning a private act of consolation into one of the most extensive surviving records of their relationship.

“Gandhi responded by setting aside time each day to write a personal thought. What began as a personal exchange soon evolved into a collaborative project,” Minal Vazirani, co-founder and president of Saffronart, told The Indian Express.

open image in gallery The handwritten messages were addressed to Anand T Hingorani, a close associate of Gandhi and a fellow participant in India’s independence movement. They were written over almost two years, and were later compiled into a book called A Thought for the Day ( Saffronart )

“While Gandhi authored each reflection, Hingorani became the recipient, organiser and transcriber, ultimately preparing the writings for publication,” she said.

The 688 entries cover many of the subjects that occupied Gandhi throughout his life, including truth, ahimsa or non-violence, brahmacharya (self-control), non-possession, fearlessness, religious equality, prayer, service, labour, duty, silence, conscience, self-realisation and the search for God.

A group of nine letters from 1930 and 1931 concerns Anand and Vidya Hingorani’s marriage, including parental opposition, financial independence, reconciliation within the family and Gandhi’s views on self-restraint and domestic obligations.

The wider collection was preserved by the Hingorani family across generations and was offered as an 86-lot sale by Saffronart under the title Gandhi: From the Collection of Anand T Hingorani.

open image in gallery The 688 entries cover many of the subjects that occupied Gandhi throughout his life, including truth, ahimsa or non-violence, brahmacharya, fearlessness, religious equality, prayer, labour, self-realisation, and the search for God ( Saffronart )

The reflections, which were the auction’s standout lot, had been estimated at Rs 150m (£1.1m) to Rs 250m (£1.9m) before the sale and eventually fetched Rs 162m (£1.2m). Saffronart said the result set a world record for an Indian historical document sold at auction.

Among the other notable lots was Message on God, a group of three manuscript and correspondence items documenting Gandhi’s reflections on God and the Bhagavad Gita, which sold for Rs 16.8m (£128,518). His peti charkha, a portable box spinning wheel, accompanied by two letters about the spiritual discipline of spinning, fetched Rs 10.2m (£78,040).

A signed presentation photograph of Gandhi writing fetched Rs 7.8m (£59,678m), while a collection of his letters, telegrams and postcards relating to economic independence sold for Rs 5.8m (£44,376m).

open image in gallery Gandhi’s peti charkha, a portable box spinning wheel, along with two letters about the spiritual discipline of spinning, sold for Rs 10.2m ( Saffronart )

“What makes this collection particularly compelling is the opportunity to see one of the most significant figures in India’s history through the lens of a close, personal relationship,” Dinesh Vazirani, co-founder of Saffronart, said in a statement.

He added that the reflections showed “how Gandhi lived the principles he advocated publicly”, describing them as a valuable record of his “thought and practice”.

The sale has also led to some concern in India over the fate of Gandhi’s original letters, manuscripts, and personal belongings. A Annamalai, director of the National Gandhi Museum in Delhi, described the auction as “deeply distressing and painful news”.

In a statement shared with The Independent, Annamalai said it is “our historical responsibility to preserve the original letters and his handwritten manuscripts”, even when their contents have already been published.

He urged those who hold such material not to sell or auction it, but to hand it over to the National Gandhi Museum so it can be preserved and made available for future generations.

“Gandhi’s letters, manuscripts and personal belongings are not merely private possessions. They are part of the common heritage of India and belong to our shared history. They should be preserved in a manner that enables people from India and across the world to see, study and learn from them,” Annamalai said.

The Independent has reached out to Saffronart for comment.

The buyer has not been identified publicly; Saffronart has confirmed they are from within India, and the manuscript will remain in the country.

Pet owners are being urged to exercise extreme caution when seeking veterinary advice on platforms like TikTok, following a warning from a leading animal charity.

The People’s Dispensary for Sick Animals (PDSA) has cautioned that popular online "hacks" and home remedies could inadvertently endanger pets’ lives.

The PDSA has seen viral clips encouraging owners to administer ibuprofen to dogs for injuries, despite the drug being highly toxic to animals.

Veterinary surgeon Cat Henstridge, who shares pet care advice to her 400,000 followers, said the golden rule is to always “run it past your vet first”.

Ms Henstridge, known online as @cat_the_vet, said: "Ibuprofen is 100 per cent off the menu for all pets and paracetamol is very toxic for cats."

open image in gallery Vets have to be ‘the first port of call’ for animal medicines ( Getty/iStock )

Whilst stressing that some general advice from social media for pets can be good, Ms Henstridge said that “when it comes to medicines, it has to be the veterinary profession that is the first port of call”.

She added: “A lot of home and herbal holistic remedies are at best ineffective and, at worse, potentially dangerous.”

Catherine Burke, a PDSA vet, said: “Animals process medications very differently from humans.

“Something safe for people can be toxic or even life-threatening for pets.”

open image in gallery The PDSA has encouraged pet lovers not ’to try home treatments seen online without first checking with their vet’ ( Getty )

Ms Burke said she can understand that social media offers pet owners “quick help”, but this comes with a risk as these viral clips often “make medical guidance appear far simpler and safer than it really is”.

The PDSA is concerned about how quickly “misinformation spreads online” and has encouraged pet lovers not “to try home treatments seen online without first checking with their vet”.

It added: “What works for one animal in a short video may not be safe for another, and similar symptoms can have very different underlying causes.”

The charity is urging owners to contact their vet directly if they are concerned about their pet’s health, rather than using social media trends or often unverified online tips.

Ms Burke added: “Following these viral tips can delay pet owners from seeking proper veterinary care, where early treatment can make a significant difference to health and wellbeing.”

The PDSA is the UK’s leading veterinary charity, with 49 pet hospitals across the UK.

The charity has a dedicated Pet Health Hub where expert advice can be found.

News.title: Arsenal play like the champions they are as title defence starts with a bang
News.content:
Good evening and welcome to the Emirates Stadium, where the Premier League champions begin the defence of their title. Or, as Mikel Arteta prefers to put it, their “attack” on a new season. A classic Arteta-ism.

The assault starts tonight against Coventry City but our understanding is that Arsenal will be without new £75m midfielder Bruno Guimaraes. We believe the Brazilian has picked up an injury, and it’s not currently clear how severe it might be. Clearly, this is a blow for Arteta. But they should still have enough to get past promoted Coventry… shouldn’t they? We’ll find out soon enough.

Meanwhile, Arteta has said he and his players should relish being Premier League title favourites and the role of the hunted rather than the hunter.

“In the last three seasons, at some point we were first and at some point we were chasing. And you never know what is better,” Arteta said. “But if you give me the choice, I want to be first. I want to be hunted, and I want to be in control of our future, rather than depending on somebody else.”

Arteta called on his players to retain the hunger they had last season.

“We start from scratch, from zero, and we’re going to have to prove we are at the level to go back to that position again,” he said. “We need to show that desire and the ambition to be better than what we were last season, a month ago, a week ago.”

This is Coventry’s first Premier League campaign since they suffered relegation in 2000-01, and they were led to the Championship title by Frank Lampard. They scored the most goals in the Championship and conceded the fewest, and could face one of their former players tonight in Viktor Gyokeres.

Full team news as and when we get it.

News.title: Russell takes Dutch GP sprint pole as Antonelli struggles to fifth
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for sprint qualifying for the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix from Zandvoort. This is the last time the race will be on the F1 calendar for the foreseeable future, having been reintroduced in 2021 after a 35-year absence. It will be a shame to see it leave again, but never rule out it coming back, especially with Max Verstappen signing a lengthy contract extension with Red Bull.

What of the competitive action this weekend? As it is a sprint weekend, there is not a lot of preparation time, with just one practice session before sprint qualifying. In that it was a fairly close fight at the top, and it was Kimi Antonelli, the championship leader, who was fastest of all. Behind him was the McLaren of Lando Norris who was 0.121sec adrift then George Russell, who will be looking to kickstart his title campaign here, a further 0.004sec behind him.

Then came the two Ferraris of Lewis Hamilton (0.190sec) and Charles Leclerc (0.289sec) before a fairly significant gap of 0.659sec to Oscar Piastri in sixth. Verstappen was down in 11th, nearly 1.4sec off Antonelli’s ultimate pace but 0.5sec or so ahead of new (and old) team-mate for the weekend, Liam Lawson.

It was a tricky session for the drivers, though, as it began damp on a showery and blustery day by the Dutch seaside. Several drivers ran wide and off the track, though they all avoided anything more serious than gravel rash. The rest of the day looks to be drier but there are still a few showers around and the wind is all over the place, as it often is here.

Sprint qualifying starts at 3.30pm BST and we will be here for all of the updates for the nearly hour-long session.

News.title: Root delivers perfect riposte to captaincy doubters as England hammer Pakistan
News.content:
There was no attempt to be a Ben Stokes tribute act by Joe Root, just a measured captaincy performance very much in his own undemonstrative style.

Root, ever the team man, pushed his bowlers forward to lead England off at the end, recognising the match-winners in a walkover against Pakistan, who were bowled out for 135 in under two sessions.

Victory by an innings and 103 runs inside three days marked a perfect return to the job and put the smile back on England faces for the first time in a long while. The chants of “F--- the ECB” from Trent Bridge, after the New Zealand regime-toppling loss, were replaced by the Yorkshire faithful’s “Roooot”.

There was plenty of scepticism around rebooting the Root captaincy, but he was the only realistic choice. Harry Brook’s batting here was more sensible and at a tempo in the captain’s mould. “He is still learning the art of Test cricket,” Root said. Thrusting Brook into the job would have put more pressure on him, he may well have felt he needed to make risky statements with the bat. Now he can mature under Root and Stephen Fleming.

Tactically, Root was astute and showed enough to suggest he is going to be different this time. The old Root would not have whipped Jofra Archer off after two overs of the Test, but it was a prod that worked as he bowled quicker and more accurately to strike twice with the second-innings new ball, using his new-found skills with a scrambled seam to good effect.

It also showed his bowlers he wanted a fuller length and, from that first hour, they controlled the match and did not let their grip slip.

Root promised to keep the good aspects of Bazball and apply common sense. He continued Stokes’s leg-slip tactic and it paid off with the wicket of opener Azan Awais, and urged Ollie Robinson to bowl with the keeper standing up. England batted at 4.5 an over – a touch quicker than the Bazball years – but it was never reckless, just a calm tempo, with no ramps or scoops.

News.title: Officials selling yellow fever certificates to unvaccinated travellers
News.content:
Officials in Malawi are selling yellow fever certificates to unvaccinated travellers for around $20 and sending them on their way, a Telegraph investigation has found.



The passport-sized, yellow document, officially called the International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP), is supposed to provide proof of vaccination against yellow fever, a mosquito-borne virus that kills tens of thousands of people every year.

The jab provides lifelong protection, beginning 10 days after vaccination. Most countries in Africa and Latin America require them for entry, either for all travellers or for those arriving from risk areas.



Yet travellers leaving Malawi through two major airports can get hold of the certificates without ever being vaccinated, according to interviews with multiple travellers and an undercover investigation.



Several passengers who travelled recently from Malawi to destinations including Uganda, Kenya, Ethiopia and China said they had obtained yellow fever vaccination certificates at airports or public hospitals without receiving the vaccine.



One traveller, who recently flew to Uganda for work from Kamuzu International Airport, which serves the capital, Lilongwe, said he was initially told it was too late to get vaccinated because his departure was less than 10 days away.



“When I asked the health officials if I could get vaccinated at the airport, I was told it was too late because I needed to be vaccinated ten days before my trip,” he told The Telegraph.



“But then they offered to arrange the certificate for me for roughly $21,” said the traveller, who asked not to be named. “I had to pay because I could not postpone the trip.”

News.title: Congo gambles on ‘old’ vaccine as new Ebola virus spirals
News.content:
Nearly half of all those infected have gone on to die.

Dr Sania Nishtar, chief executive of the Gavi global vaccine partnership, earlier this week said to beat the outbreak “we must deploy every tool at our disposal”.

She went on: “To avoid this becoming the worst recorded Ebola outbreak in history, it is critical that all effective countermeasure options are brought to bear.

“We have a tool that could help save lives while we wait for [Bundibugyo]-specific vaccines to become available.”

Previous clinical trials have shown that Ervebo is safe, but its effect on other strains is unknown.

The World Health Organisation said in a statement that while it was not known if Ervebo may protect against the Bundibugyo virus, “early laboratory and animal data suggest it may provide some protection”.

Medics told the Telegraph of anecdotal claims that health workers who had been given Ervebo to protect them during an outbreak of the Zaire strain in 2018 to 2020 had not fallen ill during the current Bundibugyo outbreak.

Health workers are at extreme risk of catching the disease because they come into contact with highly-contagious blood, vomit and diarrhoea from dying patients. When they fall sick themselves, they frequently go on to infect their own families.

Giving health workers vaccine jabs to protect them as they tend the sick is a cornerstone of Ebola responses.

The WHO said the vaccine allocation includes 20,000 doses for a Phase 3 clinical trial to understand the impact of the vaccine on the Bundibugyo virus. The remaining 50,000 doses will be used for front-line and health workers as recommended by WHO experts.

Dr Nishtar said: “Having already been licensed for the Zaire strain, we know that Ervebo is proven to be safe.

“And while the signs are that it may not stop transmission – which is essential for ending the outbreak - it could well save precious lives and reduce suffering.”

Health officials warn that the Bundibugyo outbreak centred on DRC’s Ituri province is easily outpacing relief efforts.

The virus is thought to have been spreading for months before an outbreak was finally declared in mid-May and medics have been unable to make up the head start.

An analysis by the Africa Centres for Disease Control meanwhile warned the current outbreak dwarfed all others on record

The current outbreak had almost ten times more cases than any other previous outbreak at a similar stage.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: Soaring welfare bill pushes national debt to almost £3tn
News.content:
Britain’s soaring welfare bill forced John Healey to borrow more to balance the books last month.

The gap between tax receipts and spending unexpectedly resulted in a £1.8bn deficit in July, taking the national debt to within a whisker of £3tn.

Economists had predicted the Government would borrow nothing and blamed the deficit on the rising welfare bill.

Figures published by the Office for National Statistics (ONS) this morning show total debt rose to £2.985tn in July.

Benefit payments also climbed by 7.2pc, or £2bn, to £30bn last month.

The Chancellor now faces another tax-raising Budget in October, even as strong receipts from self-employed workers provide some respite.

The ONS also said Mr Healey spent £7.7bn on debt interest in July alone, almost 10pc higher than a year ago.

Ashley Webb, at Capital Economics said: “The weak performance was mainly due higher social payments.”

Monthly borrowing was slightly higher than the Office for Budget Responsibility and markets expected, meaning the Government has borrowed £56.7bn this financial year to plug the gap between tax receipts and public spending.

Julian Jessop, an independent economist and IEA economics fellow, said: “The latest official data highlight the fragility of the public finances as John Healey prepares his first Budget. Government borrowing was £2.3bn above forecast in July, and £0.7bn higher than in the same month a year ago.”

July is traditionally a strong month for receipts from the self-employed, with self-assessed income tax receipts last month coming to £17.1bn, about £1.7bn more than a year earlier.

However, higher inflation triggered by the Iran war means Mr Healey will be forced to use the Budget to find billions of pounds to repair the public finances.

Mr Healey said: “Fiscal discipline is the bedrock of our UK economic stability and national security which is why we are committed to meeting our fiscal rules, with a buffer against global uncertainties.”

The Resolution Foundation warned that the Chancellor’s headroom against his fiscal rules - self-imposed guardrails to guide public spending - has shrunk from around £24bn in the Spring Statement to less than £8bn today.

The think tank called on the Chancellor to use his first Budget on Oct 28 to put the nation’s finances on a more sustainable path.

Elliott Christensen, senior economist at the Resolution Foundation, said: “The Chancellor’s margin against his fiscal rules is now razor thin.”

News.title: Brook falls agonisingly short of Headingley hundred again as England continue to dominate
News.content:
“Yeah, of course I did,” said Cox, when asked if he was frustrated to miss out on three figures. Cox was caught behind off spinner Ali Usman, but believed he had hit his pad with his bat, not the ball.

“Once I got to fifty, I moved to sixty quickly, and thought ‘there’s a chance here’. Just keep being disciplined, ball by ball. I had it at the back of my mind, thinking you have worked so hard, do not give this opportunity up. That is exactly what I do in county cricket. I get to fifty, see how many runs I need to score, and work down from there.”

Asked if his team-mates were feeling the same emotion, he said: “Oh yeah there is. Every team, every player wants to score Test hundreds. Four of us got fifties, so we were hoping one would kick on, and instead of making it just a hundred, make it 150 or 170.

“I am thrilled. I would have taken it at the start of the Test match. I let myself down a tiny bit, but at the end of the day, you take 70.”

Cox resumed on day two on 23, then was dropped by the bowler Khurram Shahzad on 57. In the course of his innings, he was compared to AB de Villiers by the former England captain Michael Vaughan.

Cox is likely to get a good run across formats. England had hoped to call on Sam Curran for the third Test of this series, but his summer is over due to a groin injury. Curran will undergo surgery on Friday.

It is likely England will be without Curran, Bethell and Tom Banton for September’s white-ball series against Sri Lanka, which should mean greater opportunity for the likes of Cox and Sussex’s James Coles, and could even see a recall for Zak Crawley, who made an assured 81 for Kent against Middlesex on Thursday. Will Jacks is currently sidelined with appendicitis, but is expected to have recovered in time for the series.

Sports.title: Carrick speaks out on potential Man Utd exits with Rashford, Ugarte and Zirkzee having all been strongly tipped to go
Sports.content:
MICHAEL CARRICK does not expect any Manchester United players to leave before the transfer window closes.

United have struggled to sell any senior players this summer, with goalkeeper Radek Vitek the most high-profile departure to Middlesbrough for £7million. Vitek, 22, never debuted for United.



The club were unable to shift Manuel Ugarte after he ruptured his anterior cruciate ligament at the World Cup while Barcelona opted against buying Marcus Rashford.

United would be prepared to let Joshua Zirkzee go but are not expecting any movement and Carrick revealed that even Zirkzee has not asked to leave.



“Not to me, no,” Carrick said. “I don’t know what’s going to come out. I don’t know what’s going to come at us from elsewhere.

“We can control what we can control. I’m really happy with the squad we’ve got so far, and if not, we want to improve it.”



United are keen to sign a midfielder and a left back before the 11pm deadline on September 1, having bid for Brighton enforcer Carlos Baleba.

The club enquired about Newcastle left back Lewis Hall and have been offered Arsenal youngster Myles Lewis-Skelly.

Sources expect a deal to be finalised for Baleba, 22, after United enquired about the Cameroon international a year ago.

United had always intended to bring in three midfielders this summer and signed Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos for a combined £85m last month.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Baleba is expected to command a higher fee than the initial £65m United offered, so their investment on central midfield alone would be north of £150m.

Carrick confirmed United are “working towards” another recruit to offset the release of Casemiro in June.

“As I said before, we’re trying to improve the squad all the time,” he added. “We’re working towards that.

“I think largely we’ve got a really good balance within the group. As it stands now, we’ve got some very good, top midfielders to choose from.

“So I think we’ve improved that. As I said, since the start of the window to the end, we’ll see what happens.



“We want to finish stronger as the window closes, so we’re working towards that.

“Players have always come and gone through history here, and you’ve got to evolve, you’ve got to find ways of moving forward, you’ve got to find ways of winning, essentially.

“I know we’ve got a good midfield. We’ve brought in some really, really top players and really good characters, which is important.”

United’s midfield overhaul was certain to be drastic, with Kobbie Mainoo their only senior available option heading into July.

Santos started all six pre-season friendlies and Tielemans figured in three after his post-World Cup break.



Baleba is currently nursing an ankle injury and would be unlikely to debut until next month if United can strike a deal with Brighton.

“I think the foundation of the team is important to be consistent,” Carrick explained. “To be consistent through one game from start to finish, to be consistent over a period of time.

“I think you need a solid foundation through the middle of the team and trying and putting it together and getting that balance.



“But certainly, I think if you look at all the top teams over the years, all the great teams over the years, the spine of the team is really strong.

“So we’re conscious of that, and I think we’ve got a good spine of the team right now.

“We can keep improving as we go in different ways and coaching and helping the boys and developing them, and I think we’re in a good place.”

United spent as much on Santos and Tielemans as Tottenham paid West Ham for Mateus Fernandes, United’s prime target.

After the £116m Elliot Anderson deal inflated the market, United turned to Chelsea squad player Santos and Tielemans, who had a £35m release clause.



Carrick stopped short of criticising the extreme fees paid for some midfielders but is pleased with the value of Santos and Tielemans.

“Certainly players have gone for and been more expensive,” Carrick noted. “I think that’s pretty obvious.

“We’re delighted with the two that we’ve brought in and for the money, of course.



“But actually take [the money] away, I’m delighted that we’ve got them.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Two fantastic players give us really good balance, give us a lot within the team, offer us different things.

“So, certainly, for the value that we feel we’ve got, I think we’ve done very well with those two especially.”

Sports.title: Awkward moment Gianni Infantino tries to make joke about journalist being bald when confronted about World Cup scandal
Sports.content:
INFANT BEHAVIOUR Awkward moment Gianni Infantino tries to make joke about journalist being bald when confronted about World Cup scandal

GIANNI INFANTINO awkwardly tried to make a joke about a journalist being bald as he was confronted over his World Cup scandal.

The Fifa president is still clinging on to his job despite the furious backlash to his secret plot to sell off stakes in his not-for-profit organisation’s tournaments for £20billion.

There are widespread calls for Infantino to resign and not go for re-election for a fourth term in March.



But for now the shameless Swiss remains in his post.



Dream Team is back, free, and there’s £100,000 up for grabs!

And after holing up in Morocco at the height of the crisis, Sky News tracked him down in the Dominican Republic.

Reporter James Matthews shook hands with Infantino before introducing himself.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi hit with fine after striking 22-year-old opponent in the face during MLS match
Sports.content:
LIONEL MESSI has been fined by Major League Soccer after appearing to strike an opponent in the face during Inter Miami’s draw with Philadelphia Union.

The Argentina legend, 39, was punished over an off-the-ball clash with Union attacker Quinn Sullivan, 22.



Footage circulated on social media showing the pair exchanging words near the halfway line during the second half of Wednesday’s 2-2 draw.

Messi then appeared to make contact with Sullivan’s face with his hand before referee Filip Dujic stepped in.





The eight-time Ballon d’Or winner escaped without a booking at the time and play was allowed to continue.

But MLS later announced Messi had been handed an undisclosed fine for breaching its rules regarding contact with an opponent’s face, head or neck.

It is the second time the World Cup winner has been fined by the league since joining Inter Miami in 2023.

Messi was also hit in the pocket in February 2025 following a post-match confrontation with New York City FC assistant coach Medhi Ballouchy, when he grabbed him around the neck during a heated exchange.



And his latest punishment comes just a day after Argentina were hit with a string of major Fifa sanctions over their behaviour at this summer’s World Cup.

The Argentine FA was fined £237,000 over offences including team misconduct, discriminatory chants and gestures from supporters, security breaches and the disgraceful Falklands banner displayed following their semi-final victory over England.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Argentina were also ordered to play their next two home matches with crowds limited to 50 per cent capacity.

Leandro Paredes was handed a TEN-MATCH international ban over the ugly scenes following Argentina’s World Cup final defeat to Spain, while Nahuel Molina received seven games, Thiago Almada one and assistant coach Roberto Ayala three.

Messi was not personally sanctioned during Argentina’s disgraceful behaviour at the World Cup.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford listed on programme without squad number before Man Utd announce what shirt he’ll wear this season
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED forward Marcus Rashford was listed without a squad number on the Hull City programme.

Rashford, who donned the No9 for the pre-season defeat to AC Milan last Saturday, could make his first competitive appearance for United since December 12, 2024 at newly-promoted Hull.



But the 28-year-old was the only United player without a squad number on the programme’s squad sheet.

The club later confirmed their squad numbers for the season – with Rashford being handed the No9 jersey.



Intriguingly, Shea Lacey appeared to have received an upgrade to 31 on the Hull programme, having worn 61 last term.

That was later confirmed to be the case.



It is possible that United notified Hull of Lacey’s squad number change before their editorial department went to press out of good faith.

United figures stressed last week that not all squad numbers worn in pre-season were final.

Rashford wore 14 on loan at Barcelona last season and the squad number is also free at United.

He sported the No11 for England at the World Cup and received the No9 on loan at Aston Villa last year.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

An Italian journalist claimed Rashford would receive the 14 at United but then deleted his tweet.

The number nine was vacated by misfit Rasmus Hojlund last year and Benjamin Sesko had been touted to inherit it.

However he will continue to wear the No30.

United head coach Michael Carrick has spoken glowingly about Rashford since he returned to his parent club.

“He’s come back really well. Very well,” Carrick said.



“I think the way it is now and not having so much time off really, and looking at three weeks, maybe just under three weeks, give or take.

“Boys don’t lose an awful lot in that time. It’s certainly the case of managing it coming back in though and being sensible, knowing it’s a whole season for all the players to deal with.

“So in terms of the team this week going into next week as well, getting that balance right with all the group.

“But Marcus has come back particularly bright, particularly sharp, as I’ve said, and looks really good.”

The last time United won at Hull in August 2016, Rashford scored an added-time winner off the bench.

Sports.title: Chelsea transfer window verdict with surprise key signing and Blues in need of shifting on deadwood
Sports.content:
CHELSEA have enjoyed a window full of arrivals and outgoings – but still have to do more to address their bloated squad.

The arrival of Morgan Rogers for a British-record fee was a statement of intent and brings a versatile and lethal forward to Xabi Alonso‘s side.



Moves for Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck might be less glamorous, but they add a vital element of experience and leadership to the dressing room.

But that cohesion could be undermined if too many surplus players struggle to get minutes and stagnate



Here is SunSport reporter Dan King’s verdict on the Blues’ transfer window so far…

KEY SIGNING

MORGAN ROGERS is the obvious answer — but Jordan Henderson could prove just as important.

A £117million move from Aston Villa made Rogers, 24, the most expensive British player ever.

And giving up Champions League football for at least a year was a big statement about where the England forward sees Chelsea’s potential.

If he can live up to his price tag — and shine as one of the No 10s in Xabi Alonso’s 3-4-2-1 system — the Blues’ hopes of rejoining Europe’s elite can only benefit.

The arrival of Henderson, 36, is less popular — partly due to his Liverpool background.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

But Blues bosses hope the England midfielder and fellow veteran Danny Welbeck, 35, can provide much-needed experience and leadership.

Henderson is likely to be the standard-bearer both in training and on matchday.

If he can help reduce Chelsea’s indiscipline and habit of folding under pressure, he will be worth his weight in gold.

WHAT’S MISSING OR STILL NEEDS TO BE DONE?

You can never rule out Chelsea signing players — but the emphasis is on getting bodies out of the door.

Having 40-odd senior players is way too many ahead of a campaign without European football, so it is no wonder around a dozen are training away from Alonso’s main group. But they may have to compromise on some of their price tags.



Not even Saudi side Al-Hilal are going to pay nearly £100m for Pedro Neto, while the £65m they want for Nicolas Jackson and £40m for Liam Delap are also a stretch.

They will attempt to loan out the unwanted players they cannot sell — as they have with £40m flop Alejandro Garnacho.

The biggest decision is whether to sell Enzo Fernandez with Manchester City refusing to stump up £120m.



The Blues must balance the Argentinian’s quality with the downsides of keeping someone against their will.

VERDICT

The amount of money spent and the identity of some recruits has been impressive for a club unable to offer any European football.

The Rogers signing feels like the kind of marquee name you want to kick off a new era with — and there is much-needed experience.

With Alonso favouring the setup which brought him success at Bayer Leverkusen, wing-backs Pep Chavarria and Marco Palestra have arrived.

France defender Maxence Lacroix brings quality and Prem experience.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Despite selling Trevoh Chalobah, Marc Cucurella, Tyrique George and Andrey Santos, the Blues remain over £200m in the red this summer.

So the emphasis now is on selling — and selling well.

Sports.title: Newcastle prodigy makes debut in madcap cup game with pitch invasion, riot police on horses and a 120th minute winner
Sports.content:
ALEX MURPHY made his Kaiserslautern debut in a truly mad German Cup game.

The Irish defender joined the second-division side on a season-long loan from Newcastle United earlier this month.



And he made his club bow in a volatile DFB Cup game against their bitter rivals Mannheim on Friday night.

Thousands of police were deployed for the fiery southwest derby, which was almost ABANDONED.



Dream Team is back, free, and there’s £100,000 up for grabs!

Things kicked off following a goalless 90 minutes after a brief scuffle between the players.

That lit the blue touch paper for the travelling Kaiserslautern fans to throw flares and other projectiles into the stands.

That act sparked pandemonium as hordes of Mannheim supporters STORMED the pitch.

The situation threatened to get out of control until police, some of whom were on horseback, and security intervened and removed the pitch invaders.

The incident delayed the start of extra time.

The situation was also worsened by away fans lighting a fire, which the local fire brigade managed to put out.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

A whopping 1400 police officers were deployed to keep the peace at the Carl-Benz-Stadium.

Thirty-three of them sustained injuries, with a total of 85 people requiring medical treatment.

The police, who confirmed multiple arrests, also revealed after the match that eight people were hospitalised.



Kaiserslautern booked passage to the second round with a 120th-minute goal from Ibrahim Kanate.

Murphy, 21, played 55 minutes of the cup clash, which will no doubt be ingrained in his memory for years to come.

The Irishman is looking forward to spending the season with the Red Devils, saying: “I’m very happy to be here.



“FC Kaiserslautern is a great club and I can’t wait to play my first game in this incredible stadium.

Marcus Rashford shirt number confirmed as Man Utd make JJ Gabriel decision

Marcus Rashford is likely to remain at Manchester United for the 2026-27 season after spending last term on loan at Barcelona, but he hasn't been able to reclaim his shirt number

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel and Marcus Rashford's shirt numbers have been confirmed (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United have announced that Marcus Rashford will wear the No.9 shirt this season. Rashford, who's returned to Old Trafford following a season-long loan at Barcelona, lost his No.10 shirt to Matheus Cunha last summer when it looked as if his Red Devils career was over.

‌



But the forward has now inherited another iconic shirt, with the news confirmed ahead of United's first game of the Premier League season away to newly promoted Hull on Saturday. Meanwhile, academy stars Shea Lacey and JJ Gabriel will wear No.31 and No.77 respectively.

‌



The decision to hand Rashford the No.9 shirt is further evidence that the Red Devils plan to keep him. Barcelona had the option to sign him permanently for £26million but went in a different direction.

‌



United then set a price tag of £40m but no suitor emerged. Michael Carrick is now counting on Rashford to play a key role back at his boyhood club.

Sports.title: Former Premier League referee admits players more likely to get penalty if they go down
Sports.content:
Former Premier League referee admits players more likely to get penalty if they go down

An ex-top-flight official has addressed an issue that frustrates players and fans

View 3 Images Graham Scott has given an insight into decision-making (Image: Under The Cosh)

Players are more likely to get a penalty if they hit the deck, a former Premier League referee has conceded. A frustration among many players is when fouls aren't given if they attempt to stay on their feet when they are fouled.

‌



That has resulted in players deliberately taking a tumble in a bid to force a decision from the official, which others would regard as simulation or diving. It's a thorny issue that doesn't have an obvious solution.

‌



Graham Scott, who retired as a top-level referee at the end of the 2024/25 season, has explained the difficult position officials are in. Speaking on the Under The Cosh podcast, he admitted a player going down in the event of a foul was often more likely to get the decision.

‌



After a recent example of Sunderland's Brian Bobbey not getting an obvious penalty after staying on his feet was put to him, Scott said: "There are some situations where if the player doesn't go down, they're not going to get a pen, it's as simple as that.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

"Brobbey is a very strong player, he would be difficult to ref as he also holds the other player a lot. Sometimes your assistant is telling you about holding by the other player and I say, 'Don't give anything because I can see the other player doing it from this side.'

‌



Premier League introduce nine new rules for 2026/27 season including more VAR READ MORE :

"You do get a lot of what we call mutual holding but that can also be a cop-out for not dealing with an actual foul. Clearly, if you stay on your feet, it's much less likely to be given.

"It's also much less likely to be accepted. If a referee gives a penalty against you and the player isn't even on the deck. It's like, 'Really, for that?' It works both ways."

View 3 Images An incident involving Sunderland's Brian Brobbey (left) was put to Scott (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Numerous rule tweaks have been introduced ahead of the new season, including a harder line being taken on grappling and holding at set-pieces. Referees' chief Webb insists physicality must always remain a feature of English football, but believes there were still too many instances of defenders dragging attackers to the ground last season that went unpunished.

He is keen for referees and VARs to be even more vigilant about it. Webb said: "I think fans can expect less warnings from referees [before fouls are given] than they might have seen previously, and I know [those warnings were] a source of frustration.

View 3 Images Howard Webb has explained a key change for the Premier League season (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA, Getty Images)

‌



"[Fans can expect to see] more situations being penalised, but not only in August or September, throughout the season. I'm not going to commit to say we're going to go from here to penalising lots of contact. Contact's still part of the game.

"We still maintain a high threshold, but I would imagine we'll be sat here this time next year and we’ll be able to reflect on a season where more offences have been penalised. There'll be subtle actions that aren’t penalised, which are all part of the game, we are looking at those clear actions that are clearly unfair."

Sports.title: Arsenal star Bukayo Saka sets record straight on injury battle and sends Ezri Konsa message
Sports.content:
Arsenal star Bukayo Saka sets record straight on injury battle and sends Ezri Konsa message

Bukayo Saka started and scored in Arsenal's 3-0 Premier League triumph over Coventry on Friday evening, putting concerns over his fitness after a patchy World Cup firmly to bed

View 3 Images Bukayo Saka is over his injury problems

Arsenal star Bukayo Saka insists his World Cup injury frustration is already a distant memory. The 24-year-old marksman had to manage Achilles' pain carefully at the back end of last season and throughout this summer's tournament in North America.

‌



However, Saka has hit the ground running in the Premier League, starting and scoring for the champions in their 3-0 demolition of Coventry.

‌



He claims the secret to his sharpness is not prolonged rest - but even more training - explaining: "The World Cup was a couple of months ago, but I've put in a lot of work since then. It was more about balancing my time off and not having too much of a break.

‌



"So, I took seven days off and then I started to train again. I'm just trying to come back in good shape so I'm on top of my game."

Saka's stunning hat-trick in the electric 6-4 third-place play-off victory over France in Miami ignited the fire within his belly for the new season. It's partially why he refused to take his foot off the gas, especially as his condition gradually improved during the World Cup.

He admits it was a challenging and mentally-taxing summer, so much so that he reported back to London Colney for pre-season training two days early. The tricky dribbler continued: "Yeah, it was [difficult].

"It didn't necessarily go how I wanted it to. Myself and for the team as well. But, yeah, I put the World Cup behind me mentally and just worked on the team."

‌



Arsenal are now reaping the rewards of his hunger, and he has one mission on his mind: retaining the club's domestic crown. Saka said: "That's the mindset. We want to do it again, and we're going to give our best."

View 3 Images Bukayo Saka rifled in Arsenal's second goal against Coventry

After Mikel Arteta's Gunners netted all three goals from open play, the efficient right-winger was quizzed on whether we are going to see 'a more attacking Arsenal' this season.

‌



The England international responded sternly: "I don't like this narrative, to be honest. I think it's a great start for the team. We played beautiful football and we scored, what the game required. Sometimes it's a set piece, sometimes it's open play. It's about winning and that's what matters."

Saka knew there was somebody special waiting for him as soon as he left the field. It was his close friend, Ezri Konsa. The pair have struck a unique bond while playing together for England - Konsa even FaceTimed Saka from Aston Villa's open-top bus Europa League parade - and now they are team-mates at club level.

View 3 Images Bukayo Saka (right) and Ezri Konsa (left) are close friends

‌



The 28-year-old centre-back has joined the Gunners in a deal worth an initial £51million plus £4m in add-ons and was in attendance to watch Arsenal romp their way to victory while securing the first of many clean sheets this season.

Saka can't wait to see Konsa pull on the red and white shirt. He said when asked to explain their bromance: "I don't know how to describe it, man. Ever since I met him at England, we've just got on.

"Yeah, I'm so happy to have him here. Not only because he's a brother to me, but I know the level of player he is and I'm excited for him to show it at this level."

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Next signing after Carlos Baleba decided as Myles Lewis-Skelly verdict reached
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Next signing after Carlos Baleba decided as Myles Lewis-Skelly verdict reached

As Manchester United prepare for their Premier League opener, there is still time for Michael Carrick to add to his squad

View 2 Images Carlos Baleba might not be the last signing to join Manchester United this summer (Image: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

The wait is over for Manchester United fans. No, not for their latest transfer, but rather for their first Premier League action of the new season.

‌



Another addition might not be too far away, though. Michael Carrick won't have Carlos Baleba in his squad in time for Saturday's lunchtime kick-off against Hull City but progress is being made on a deal for the Brighton star.

‌



Baleba looks set to join Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans among United's midfield options and the Cameroonian might not be the last new addition. There's still more than a week to get deals done and that leaves time for plenty of movement.

‌



We've also got an update on Myles Lewis-Skelly, whose name has been mentioned in connection with a United switch this summer. Here are our latest lines from around Old Trafford.

Coleen Rooney beams with joy as she reveals Man Utd starlet son Kai's GCSE results READ MORE :

Next move after Baleba

United are expected to explore a move for a new left-back once they have completed their move for Carlos Baleba, according to the Manchester Evening News. There are still some final touches to be made to the Baleba deal but soon attentions can be turned elsewhere.

‌



Luke Shaw remains United's first choice in the position but the extra toll of Champions League football means there may well be a desire for someone who can provide immediate competition and the quality to succeed the England international in the long-term.

View 2 Images Alejandro Balde is among the left-backs to be linked with an Old Trafford switch (Image: Urbanandsport/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)
