World.title: More Czech Companies Test Four-Day Work Weeks Despite Political Resistance
World.content:
A growing number of companies in the Czech Republic are experimenting with a four-day working week, with some reporting higher productivity and greater employee satisfaction.

But politicians remain reluctant to make the arrangement a standard option across the country.

Under the model, employees work four days instead of five while keeping their full salaries. Companies that have introduced the system say workers can maintain their output while having more time to rest.



At Trinity Group, the arrangement has been in place for five years. Jan Hanulík, the company’s product and marketing director, said productivity had risen despite employees working one day less each week.

“Although we have one working day less, productivity has increased,” Hanulík said, adding that the company’s results have roughly doubled since the system was introduced.

A survey cited in the report found that around 70 percent of employees in the Czech Republic would welcome a four-day working week.

Politicians remain cautious

The idea has already been adopted in different forms elsewhere in Europe. In Belgium, for example, employees can request to work their weekly hours over four days rather than five. The system therefore does not necessarily mean fewer working hours.

Czech politicians, however, argue that a single system would not work across all sectors.

Labor and Social Affairs Minister Aleš Juchelka of ANO said a legally mandated four-day week could create problems in areas already facing staff shortages, including social services and health care.

SPD lawmaker Lucie Šafránková also said the working week should reflect the conditions of individual professions and employers rather than follow one nationwide rule.

Czech companies are already experimenting

Several companies have introduced or tested four-day schedules, including SAB Finance, Phonexia, Sherpas, Digiskills and Café Eternity.

Not every experiment has lasted. The Cognito agency eventually returned to a traditional five-day working week after testing the shorter schedule.

World.title: Foreign Workers Now Make Up 22% of Czech Employees
World.content:
Foreign workers accounted for around 22% of all employees in the Czech Republic at the end of 2025, according to data from the Czech National Bank (ČNB).

Their number has nearly tripled over the past decade, rising from about 323,000 in 2015 to 935,000 last year.

The increase has significantly changed the makeup of the Czech labor market. Foreign workers represented roughly 8% of all employees in 2015. By the end of 2025, their share had reached 22%.

Ukrainians made up the largest group of foreign employees, with approximately 358,000 working in Czechia at the end of last year. Slovaks were the second-largest group, numbering almost 230,000.



The Czech labor market has also seen increasing numbers of workers from other countries outside the European Union, including the Philippines and India.

Foreign workers are particularly important in several sectors, including manufacturing, construction, retail, transport and hospitality.

Their presence is most pronounced in accommodation, food services and hospitality. Foreign nationals accounted for more than half of all employees in the sector at the end of 2025.

The figures should, however, be interpreted with some caution when comparing individual industries. The CNB notes that employment agencies can distort the sectoral breakdown.

Workers employed through agencies are recorded in official statistics under administrative and support services, even when their actual jobs are in manufacturing, construction, logistics or other industries.

World.title: Tesco Teams Up With Wolt. Can Express Delivery Save Its Czech Business?
World.content:
Tesco will launch a new express delivery service in Prague in September, working with Wolt to deliver orders within 40 minutes.

The service, called Tesco Hned, will initially be available from selected Tesco stores in the Czech capital.

The launch comes as speculation continues over a possible sale of Tesco’s Central European operations and the British retailer’s future in the Czech Republic.



Tesco Hned is designed for customers who need groceries and other everyday products quickly rather than as part of a larger planned shop. Orders will include food, drinks, cosmetics, household products, pet supplies and other goods.

The company says its standard online shopping service will continue to focus on larger orders, while the new option is aimed at customers who need a few items immediately.

Tesco has already tested the service at six Prague stores. It plans to extend Tesco Hned to another 22 locations in the coming weeks.

Delivery will be provided through Wolt, giving customers access to Tesco products through the courier company’s platform.

Tesco faces questions over its future

The new service comes at a difficult time for Tesco in Central Europe.

According to the Financial Times, Tesco’s British owners are considering selling their operations in the region, including the Czech Republic. The Schwarz Group, which owns Lidl and Kaufland, and Polish retailer Biedronka have reportedly been mentioned among potential buyers.

Tesco has not announced plans to leave the Czech market, and the launch of Tesco Hned suggests the company continues to invest in its services.

World.title: New Budget Airline to Launch Direct Flights from Prague to Santiago de Compostela
World.content:
A new budget airline is set to launch direct flights between Prague and Santiago de Compostela in Spain, giving travellers from the Czech capital a new low-cost option for visiting Galicia and the famous Camino de Santiago.

Fly2Galicia plans to begin operating flights from Santiago–Rosalía de Castro Airport to eight European destinations from December 1, 2026.



Prague is among the international destinations, alongside Brussels, Munich, Venice and Milan.

Tickets are already on sale, with fares from Prague to Santiago de Compostela starting at €51.

The new route could be particularly attractive in 2027, when Santiago de Compostela will celebrate a Holy Year. The occasion is expected to bring increased numbers of pilgrims completing the Camino de Santiago, one of Europe’s best-known pilgrimage routes.

There is, however, one detail to note: Fly2Galicia will not operate the initial flights itself. The airline says the routes will be operated by another European carrier, which has not yet been named.

The new service comes as airlines continue to expand connections between Central Europe and Spain. Wizz Air has also announced new flights to Santiago from Rome and Warsaw starting this December.

What to see in Santiago de Compostela

For travellers arriving from Prague, Santiago’s historic centre is the main attraction. Its UNESCO-listed Old Town combines Romanesque, Gothic, Baroque and Neoclassical architecture, with the Cathedral of Santiago at the heart of the city.

The Mercado de Abastos is another popular stop, offering fresh seafood and local produce. Galicia is also known for Albariño, a white wine that pairs particularly well with the region’s seafood.

Santiago can also serve as a base for exploring Galicia, with trips to A Coruña, Vigo and the Rías Baixas wine region, as well as the area’s beaches and islands.

World.title: Russell Crowe to Perform in Prague for the First Time in May 2027
World.content:
Oscar-winning actor and musician Russell Crowe will bring his band, The Gentlemen Barbers, to Forum Karlín on May 23, 2027, for their first-ever Prague concert.

Russell Crowe is best known for his roles in Gladiator, A Beautiful Mind and A Good Year, but long before Hollywood, music was a major part of his life.

On May 23, 2027, the Oscar and Golden Globe winner will bring that side of his career to Prague for the first time, performing with his band The Gentlemen Barbers at Forum Karlín.



You can get your ticket here.

The concert will also mark the opening night of the band’s European tour.

The Gentlemen Barbers have been developing their sound over the past four years, although many of the musicians have worked with Crowe for decades. The lineup includes drummer Dave Kelly and trumpeter Stewart Kirwan, both former members of Thirty Odd Foot of Grunts, as well as musicians who have collaborated with Crowe on later projects.

The band also features pianist Stu Hunter, guitarist Chris Kamzelas and bassist James Hazelwood. Irish singer Lorraine O’Reilly, known for her powerful, raspy vocals, has performed with Crowe since they first met while recording a duet for the Bible Code Sundays album Walk Like Kings.

The result is a band that moves between R&B, gospel, country, dark waltzes and singalong anthems, with storytelling at the centre of its music.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by JV Classics (@jvclassics)

“There is an attitude about this band. It’s got a groove. We do a lot of story songs, but we also know we are here to blow out cobwebs and give the audience a good night,” Crowe says.

For Crowe, music has remained a constant alongside his film career. He began performing in bands, touring and releasing records before moving into musical theatre and eventually film. He has continued to perform throughout his decades in Hollywood, despite his demanding acting career.

“I love playing in pubs. It’s what I did growing up. Even though my day job has a huge claim on my time, I’ve never not played music,” he says.

Russell Crowe’s Indoor Garden Party & The Gentlemen Barbers takes place on May 23, 2027, at 8 p.m. at Forum Karlín in Prague.

World.title: Students in Czech Republic Face Higher Rents as Housing Costs Rise
World.content:
Students looking for private accommodation in Czech university cities this year are facing higher rents, with prices for some types of housing up by as much as 14 percent compared with 2025.

The increase comes as demand for student accommodation reaches its annual peak ahead of the winter semester.

Data from several Czech property platforms show that the busiest period started earlier this year, meaning students who have not yet found accommodation may face a more limited and expensive selection in September.

Those unable to secure a place in a student dormitory generally have three alternatives: renting a small apartment alone, taking a private room in a shared apartment, or renting a bed in shared accommodation.



The most expensive option is usually a small one-bedroom apartment with a kitchenette, typically around 30 square meters. According to the REMAX network, monthly rents for these apartments range from more than CZK 7,000 in Ústí nad Labem to around CZK 14,000 in Prague.

Prices have not increased evenly across the country. Brno recorded the sharpest rise, with rents for small apartments increasing by 12 percent year on year.

Prague saw a 4 percent increase, while rents in Hradec Králové and Pardubice rose by almost 9 percent. Olomouc was one of the few exceptions, with prices falling by slightly more than 2 percent.

Rent is not the only expense students need to consider. Utilities, water and maintenance charges can add another CZK 1,000 to CZK 2,000 a month, according to property platforms.

Private rooms offer a cheaper alternative

Many students instead rent individual rooms in shared apartments, with properties ranging from smaller 2+kk and 2+1 layouts to larger 4+kk and 4+1 apartments. Czech property portal Sreality.cz puts the average cost of a private room in university cities at between approximately CZK 5,700 in Opava and CZK 11,500 in Prague.

In Prague, private rooms listed on Sreality.cz were around 10 percent more expensive than during the same period last year. Prices in Brno, meanwhile, remained roughly unchanged.

Shared housing remains the cheapest option

For students on a tighter budget, sharing an apartment and renting a bed rather than an entire room remains the least expensive choice. The more people share a property, the lower the individual housing costs tend to be.

Even this option, however, has become more expensive. According to UlovDomov.cz, the cost of renting a bed has increased by several hundred Czech crowns compared with last year.

Prague remains considerably more expensive. A bed in a two-bedroom apartment costs almost CZK 5,500, about CZK 1,200 more than a bed in a three-bedroom apartment.

World.title: 58 Years Since Warsaw Pact Troops Invaded Czechoslovakia
World.content:
On August 21, 1968, Soviet troops and their Warsaw Pact allies invaded Czechoslovakia to bring an end to that country’s brief period of political liberalization, called the Prague Spring.

People still recall waking up on that fateful morning to find that Soviet-led Warsaw Pact tanks had rolled into the country, crushing all hope of implementing the democratic reforms of the Prague Spring. Shocked citizens took to the streets in protest of the invasion.

About 500,000 troops were involved in the invasion and occupation, during which 137 Czechoslovaks died and some 500 were wounded.

One of the key battles was for the control of Czech Radio, similar to the one that took place at the end of the Second World War.

The invasion ended the political and economic reforms led by Alexander Dubcek and reasserted dominant Soviet and Communist authority in Czechoslovakia.

It also helped establish the Brezhnev Doctrine, which Moscow said allowed the U.S.S.R. to intervene in any country where a communist government was under threat.

Within the following year, resistance faded, Dubček was removed from office, his reforms were undone, and a more Soviet-controlled government was installed.

World.title: Prague’s Groovy Market Fest Returns After a Successful Debut
World.content:
A new urban festival is aiming to become a regular fixture on Prague’s cultural calendar after attracting 1,200 visitors to its first edition in Riegrovy sady.

Groovy Market Fest, held on August 1, brought together food, design, music and local brands in a format inspired by European city markets.

According to the organizers, around 85% of visitors were tourists or foreign residents of Prague, highlighting the event’s appeal beyond the Czech-speaking audience.



The festival will return to Riegrovy sady on September 5, with further editions planned for October, November and December.

From Barcelona to Prague

Groovy Market Fest was founded by Marek Novák and Veronika Kracíková, a couple with experience in Prague’s food scene and Barcelona’s street-food culture.

Their interest in international gastronomy also led them to compete in Spain. In 2025, they won first place in the Cooking The Street competition, where their dish was judged by a professional panel that included chefs Beñat Ormaetxea and Jon Kepa Aurrecoetxea.

After returning to Prague, they decided to develop their own event, drawing inspiration from markets such as Barcelona’s Palo Alto Market.

The First Edition

Food Garden focused on gastronomy, while Palm Street featured local products and handmade goods. The Design Zone presented Czech brands working in fashion, design and art.

Rather than filling the site with as many vendors as possible, the organizers selected a smaller number of participants. They say the approach was intended to create a more coherent experience for visitors.

Music was another part of the programme, with live performances and DJ sets throughout the event. Visitors could also attend a masterclass focused on preparing the festival’s signature Groovy cocktail.

Additional editions are scheduled for October 3, November 7 and December 5, all at the same location.

Tickets for upcoming editions are available through GoOut.

World.title: Tropical fever disease has appeared in Hungary
World.content:
An imported case of the disease called chikungunya fever has been confirmed in Bács-Kiskun County, Hungary after an 53-year-old woman returned from Mauritius, according to Hungary’s latest weekly epidemiological report.

The National Public Health and Pharmaceutical Centre (NNGYK) recorded the laboratory-confirmed case during the 32nd epidemiological week, covering 3–9 August 2026. The woman was in Mauritius during the infection’s incubation period and is believed to have contracted the virus there.

What kind of disease is chikungunya fever?

Chikungunya is a viral disease transmitted primarily through the bites of infected mosquitoes. The main vectors are the Aedes aegypti, or yellow fever mosquito, and the Aedes albopictus, commonly known as the Asian tiger mosquito.

The infection does not spread directly from person to person without a mosquito acting as an intermediary. Around one-third of infected people may remain symptom-free. In those who develop symptoms, the incubation period is generally several days, after which the illness can cause:

sudden, high fever;

severe joint pain;

headaches;

muscle pain; and

an occasional skin rash.

Most patients begin to recover within a week, and the fatality rate is extremely low. However, more serious complications can pose a greater risk to older people, newborn babies and those with weakened immune systems, according to the NNGYK.

Imported chikungunya cases remain uncommon in Hungary, with only a small number of travel-related infections generally recorded each year.

Malaria case also linked to overseas travel

The same weekly report recorded another imported tropical infection. An 18-year-old man living in Pest County was diagnosed with malaria after spending time in Tanzania during the disease’s incubation period.

Laboratory testing identified Plasmodium falciparum as the causative parasite. This species is responsible for the most severe form of malaria and can require urgent medical treatment.

This might interest you: How to see a doctor without insurance in Budapest — a tourist’s guide

Gastroenteritis outbreak affects 54 people

The NNGYK report also documented a larger outbreak unrelated to overseas travel. An enteric outbreak occurred at a hotel in Zala County, where 54 of 640 exposed people became ill between 1 August and the publication of the report. Those affected included 50 hotel guests and four members of staff.

Vomiting and diarrhoea were the main symptoms. They reportedly disappeared within a short period, and most of those affected did not require medical attention.

Hungary’s public health authorities publish weekly epidemiological reports to monitor infectious diseases across the country and identify outbreaks and imported infections. The latest figures highlight how international travel can occasionally introduce diseases that are otherwise rarely encountered in Hungary.

World.title: Major Budapest railway upgrade that could reshape commuting just got revealed
World.content:
A major railway development could transform commuting between Budapest and several surrounding towns, with HUF 174 billion (appr. EUR 480 million) earmarked for the modernisation of the Budapest–Fót–Veresegyház–Őrbottyán–Vác railway line.

The investment is part of the Baross Gábor Railway Development Plan and will be financed from the EU Cohesion Fund through the IKOP Plus programme. The aim is to create a faster, more frequent and accessible suburban railway service by 2030.

Up to six trains an hour

According to Dávid Vitézy, Minister for Transport and Investment, the upgrade is increasingly necessary as more residents of the affected settlements commute to Budapest. Most currently travel by car, contributing to congestion, air pollution and demand for parking in the capital.

The upgraded railway is expected to provide a more attractive alternative. In the Fót, Veresegyház and Őrbottyán area, the current service of around one or two trains per hour could increase to four to six trains an hour. A second track will be built where necessary and feasible, increasing capacity and allowing more frequent services. Stations and stops will also be renovated and made accessible, while new P+R car parks and B+R facilities for cyclists will make it easier for commuters to combine different modes of transport.

Passenger numbers could quadruple

Earlier modelling for the Budapest Agglomeration Railway Strategy suggested that passenger numbers on the Veresegyház line could eventually reach three to four times their current level. The line already carries around 10,000 passengers despite its limited service, with trains frequently becoming crowded.

Experience from previously upgraded routes towards Esztergom and Székesfehérvár shows the potential impact of investment, with passenger numbers on those lines reportedly almost doubling. Surveys have also indicated that many more commuters would choose suburban rail if services improved in both quality and frequency.

More on Budapest: How the busiest Budapest metro line cannot be extended far enough because of the Russians

Connection to the M3 metro

The railway project is part of a broader transport development programme. Rákospalota–Újpest station is also due to be upgraded, while plans envisage extending the M3 metro to the station. The railway, station development and metro extension are all intended to be completed by 2030, creating a stronger connection between Budapest’s suburban rail network and the underground system.

Vitézy also said he and his colleagues had worked on the Veresegyház line’s development while he was head of the Budapest Development Centre, but claimed the project was later halted by János Lázár. If delivered as planned, the investment could make rail a far more competitive alternative to driving for residents of Budapest’s rapidly growing northern suburbs.

World.title: Hungary’s most bizarre 20 August monument? Devecser unveils a winged penis sculpture – photos
World.content:
A small Hungarian town has found an unmistakable way to commemorate one of the country’s darkest historical tragedies – by unveiling a winged penis sculpture.

The unusual wooden monument was unveiled in Devecser, western Hungary, on 20 August as part of the town’s national holiday celebrations. It was installed in the town’s Memorial Park in remembrance of the Battle of Mohács, the devastating 1526 defeat that marked a turning point in Hungarian history.

At first glance, the sculpture might look like an unconventional historical monument. A closer look, however, leaves little doubt about what it depicts.

A very unusual historical symbol

The sculpture portrays a winged male sexual organ, a symbol that may have a surprisingly long history. According to 444.hu, winged phalluses were popular amulets in ancient Rome. Such bronze objects were believed to protect their owners against illness, the evil eye and curses.

That historical association may offer at least one explanation for the choice of symbol in Devecser – particularly given the town’s decision to dedicate the monument to the catastrophic defeat at Mohács.

The Battle of Mohács took place in 1526, when the Hungarian army suffered a devastating defeat against the Ottoman forces. King Louis II was killed and much of the Hungarian nobility and military leadership was wiped out in the battle.

Your story. Your perspective. Our readers. Write for Daily News Hungary!

Local officials behind the unusual monument

The idea for the sculpture and the drawings used to create it reportedly came from Hajnalka Nyárs, deputy mayor of Devecser. The wooden carving itself was made by Róbert Kardos, mayor of the nearby village of Bodorfa.

The monument was formally blessed during Devecser’s 20 August celebrations, marking Hungary’s national holiday. During the ceremony, Nyárs thanked those who work for the local community, including teachers, healthcare workers, people serving the public and those who work quietly behind the scenes. She also highlighted the importance of families, saying that the family is the foundation of every community.

From ancient amulet to modern monument

While the sculpture is certainly an unusual way to commemorate the Battle of Mohács, its creators may have drawn on the ancient belief that winged phallic symbols could ward off misfortune and evil. Whatever the original intention, the monument has already attracted considerable attention online, and is unlikely to be confused with a conventional historical memorial anytime soon.

World.title: Fidesz communications chief files criminal complaint over unpaid severance
World.content:
Bertalan Havasi, opposition Fidesz’s communications director, has filed a complaint with the Budapest Investigative Prosecutor’s Office for abuse of office after failing to receive his pay during the severance period following his dismissal in May.

According to a letter seen by MTI, lawyer Róbert Répássy, a former state secretary at the justice ministry, filed the complaint on Havasi’s behalf against the former deputy state secretary for abuse of office.

Havasi, a former deputy state secretary at the Prime Minister’s Office, was dismissed by Prime Minister Péter Magyar on 16 May with immediate effect. His government service contract was set to expire on Nov 16, including a six-month severance period starting 17 May, during which he was exempt from work obligations and entitled to monthly severance payments.

Your story. Your perspective. Our readers. Write for Daily News Hungary!

Zsuzsanna Ducsay, the state secretary of administration at the Prime Minister’s Office, had previously informed Havasi in a letter that she would arrange for the calculation and payment of his severance and other benefits, as well as the issuance of required certifications. However, Havasi’s July severance payment was not made, according to the complaint.

The document also notes that Magyar had publicly said on at least two occasions that Havasi’s severance pay would not be paid.

World.title: Pro-Palestinian and pro-Israel demonstrations held simultaneously in Central Budapest
World.content:
Two opposing demonstrations took place simultaneously in central Budapest on Friday afternoon, with a pro-Palestinian solidarity rally held near the Central Market Hall and a pro-Israel demonstration organised outside the Dohány Street Synagogue.

Both events began at 2 PM, reflecting the sharply divided views surrounding the war in Gaza and the wider Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

Pro-Palestinian protesters call for freedom and peace

The pro-Palestinian demonstration took place on Vámház Boulevard and was organised by the Community of Palestinians Living in Hungary.

According to Euronews, participants expressed solidarity with Palestinians detained by Israel, particularly Dr Husam Abu Safiya, a paediatrician and obstetrician who, according to organisers, has been held without charge or trial since 2024.

Demonstrators called for freedom for Palestine and a genuine peace in the Middle East. A small number of counter-protesters carrying Israeli flags were also present.

One participant accused Israel of presenting itself as a victim while Palestinians were being detained and called for the country’s international isolation. Another questioned why Hungary continued to maintain relations with Israel.

Photo: MTI

Pro-Israel rally held near Budapest synagogue

At the same time, a separate demonstration was held outside the Dohány Street Synagogue, where participants said they were standing up for the rights and security of Hungary’s Jewish community and expressing solidarity with Israel.

One participant said the demonstration was intended to make clear that Hungary should not allow rallies supporting Hamas. The participant argued that the pro-Palestinian demonstration was not simply about supporting Palestinian civilians, but also amounted to support for a person described as a terrorist.

The two demonstrations took place within the same central Budapest area, with opposing groups expressing sharply different interpretations of the conflict and the status of Palestinian detainees.

Photo: MTI

Israel rejects portrayal of Abu Safiya as a political prisoner

Israel’s ambassador to Hungary, Maya Kadosh, addressed the issue in a video message earlier this week. She said the organisers of the pro-Palestinian demonstration “support terrorism” and argued that the Hungarian public has a right to know the facts before Abu Safiya is portrayed as an iconic hero.

According to Kadosh and Israeli government-linked sources, Abu Safiya is a Hamas colonel who was detained by Israel based on intelligence information and is being held lawfully.

The status and treatment of Abu Safiya have been strongly disputed, making his case a focal point of the competing demonstrations in Budapest. The protests also mark a change from the policy of Hungary’s previous government, under which pro-Palestinian or pro-Hamas demonstrations were not permitted in Hungary.

World.title: Hungary split in two: More than 10°C separates the hottest and coolest parts of the country
World.content:
Hungary is experiencing a striking weather divide on Friday, with temperatures varying by more than 10°C between the country’s coolest and hottest regions. A wavy frontal system is bringing heavy showers and thunderstorms to western and northern Hungary, while the southeast is sweltering in temperatures approaching 40°C.

21°C in the west, almost 39°C in the southeast

The contrast was already clear around midday and remained pronounced throughout the day. According to Időkép, the highest temperature recorded on Friday was 38.7°C near Kötegyán in Békés County, while the instruments at Kendig Peak in the west showed just 21.36°C. The national average was around 32°C.

The sharp contrast is being driven by the frontal system crossing the country. While sunny and mostly dry conditions prevail across much of the southeast, cloudier and stormier weather is affecting the west and north.

Storms and torrential rain expected

HungaroMet forecasts several waves of showers and thunderstorms moving from southwest towards northeast across northern and western parts of the country.

Thunderstorms may bring strong or locally severe wind gusts, hail and intense rainfall. Conditions are particularly favourable for severe storms in Transdanubia, where storm systems could develop with very strong winds, larger hail and torrential downpours.

The weather service has issued warnings for thunderstorms in western and northern counties, as well as for torrential rain in four western counties. Heat-related warnings are also in place in four counties in the Southern Great Plain. Thunderstorm activity is expected to decrease towards late evening, although another, weaker band of showers and thunderstorms may arrive from the west later at night.

If you missed it: Severe storms threaten several regions in Hungary, heat to peak today

Weekend brings cooler temperatures

Temperatures will fall to between 21 and 30°C by late Friday evening. Saturday will be noticeably cooler, with daytime highs generally between 25 and 33°C. Sunday morning will bring temperatures of around 13–20°C, while afternoon highs are expected to reach 24–31°C.

The heat will gradually return in the following days, with daytime temperatures rising again in some parts of the country. HungaroMet currently expects highs of 28–34°C on Thursday. For now, however, Hungary remains divided between stormy, significantly cooler conditions in the west and another spell of intense summer heat in the southeast.

World.title: Hungary’s PM Magyar reveals what moved him to tears on 20 August
World.content:
Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar has revealed which moment of this year’s 20 August national holiday left the strongest impression on him, highlighting a meeting with 160 young people from child protection institutions.

In a Facebook post on Friday, Magyar described the national holiday as a long, memorable and heartwarming day, but said that meeting the young people shortly before the evening fireworks was by far its most emotional moment.

‘Heartbreaking and uplifting’

The 160 young people had been invited to the Karmelita Palace, where they watched the fireworks from the terrace while enjoying food and refreshments. Magyar said he briefly sat down with the young people on the grass and spoke with them before the fireworks began.

He described seeing the young people as both “heartbreaking and uplifting”, noting that although they had faced difficult circumstances, they were smiling and enjoying the national holiday.

The prime minister also made a pointed political reference to the location, saying that the young people were having a picnic in the same place where, a year earlier, “those in power who had abandoned them and believed themselves untouchable” had celebrated.

“I thought to myself that there is justice. Love ultimately conquers everything,” Magyar wrote.

Your story. Your perspective. Our readers. Write for Daily News Hungary!

A 16-hour national holiday

Magyar also recounted his packed schedule on 20 August, saying that he left the main entrance of Parliament at 8 AM for the swearing-in ceremony and returned to the same location 16 hours later, at midnight, to bid farewell to tens of thousands of young people celebrating.

His programme included the raising of the national flag, the swearing-in ceremony for newly commissioned officers, an air show and the presentation of state awards. He also attended the national meeting of TISZA Islands, which he said brought together around 10,000 supporters, as well as the procession carrying the Holy Right at St Stephen’s Basilica.

The evening programme included a large-scale drone show and light display, along with Hungarian carnival events at three locations. Yet, despite the packed programme, Magyar said his meeting with the 160 young people was the moment he would remember most from this year’s national holiday.

World.title: Polish bus driver speaks out after deadly Hungary crash: ‘No words can ease the families’ pain’
World.content:
The Polish coach driver involved in the deadly bus crash on Hungary’s M3 motorway has expressed his condolences to the victims and their families through his lawyer, saying he is aware of the immense weight and consequences of the tragedy.

In a statement released on Thursday evening, lawyer Dániel Gerván told the Hungarian News Agency (MTI) that his client understands that no words can ease the loss suffered by the victims’ families. The driver has been deeply affected by the crash and is receiving professional help to process what happened, his lawyer said.

Investigation still at an early stage

Gerván stressed that the criminal proceedings are still at a very early stage. In view of the ongoing investigation, the defence is not currently releasing further details about the circumstances of the crash.

The lawyer added that the family would share further information with the public through their legal representative in the future. The driver has been detained and is being investigated on suspicion of causing a fatal mass accident through negligence. A court ordered his detention earlier this week.

Photo: MTI

Twelve people died in M3 motorway crash

The tragedy happened in the early hours of 16 August near Mezőkeresztes, when a Polish coach carrying pilgrims left the road and overturned onto its side. There were 59 people on board, including 57 passengers and two drivers. Twelve people were killed, while dozens of others suffered injuries.

According to prosecutors, three people sustained life-threatening injuries, while another 20 suffered serious injuries expected to take more than eight days to heal. Eight others were also injured. The injured passengers were taken to hospitals in Miskolc, Debrecen, Nyíregyháza and Eger. The first group of around 20 injured passengers returned to Poland on Monday evening.

Read more details: 12 killed in devastating bus crash on Hungary’s M3 motorway

Driver allegedly fell asleep at the wheel

According to the prosecutor’s office, the driver was not in a condition to operate the coach safely because of fatigue and allegedly fell asleep while driving. The bus subsequently left the carriageway via the emergency lane and overturned on a sloping section of land.

Initial police information indicated that the driver may have fallen asleep. According to Telex, investigators estimated from the scene that he may have been asleep for between two and four seconds, although a vehicle engineering expert, Sándor Boncsér, said that even less time could be enough for a 24-tonne coach to become uncontrollable if its driver falls asleep.

The investigation is continuing, and the exact circumstances that led to the crash have not yet been established with complete certainty.

World.title: Less than half of Romanians manage to save regularly, survey finds
World.content:
Roughly 48% of Romanians are able to put away money every month or most months, while a quarter manage to put money aside only occasionally, when they have funds left, according to a survey conducted at the initiative of tbi bank on a sample of 1,223 employees nationwide.

The survey, published on Friday, August 21, shows that Romanians’ real savings capacity remains limited and vulnerable to increasing pressures on the monthly budget.

Roughly 22% of respondents currently do not save at all or are forced to draw on previously accumulated reserves. Moreover, about 46% manage to save no more than RON 500 in a typical month, and 16% are unable to set aside any money at all.

The ability to save remains moderate even among those who manage to put money aside: almost 22% save between 11% and 20% of income, and just over 22% manage to keep between 6% and 10%.

“For many Romanians, saving remains the result of a fragile balance at the end of the month rather than a consistent financial plan. The increase in essential costs limits the amounts available, and this makes financial discipline, access to simple and safe products and the formation of savings habits increasingly important,” said Gergana Staykova, Market Leader, tbi bank Romania.

The ability to save has deteriorated for an important part of Romanians in the last period. Almost 42% say they save less than last year, and over 9% managed to put money aside previously, but currently they can no longer do so. At the same time, more than 29% save primarily for unforeseen situations or emergencies, and about 20% aim to build more security and financial independence.

Over 36% say they save only what they have left after covering expenses, while only about 15% set aside a fixed percentage of their monthly income. At the same time, almost 23% could cover their expenses for less than a month if they lost their main source of income, and about 22% could cover their expenses for between one and three months.

Romanians keep their savings mainly in forms perceived as safe and easy to access. Over 23% keep most of their savings in their current account, and almost 22% choose bank deposits. At the same time, more than 26% point to the increase in the price of food and basic products as the main obstacle to saving, and almost 25% say that income is too low in relation to expenses.

Savings are used both for planned experiences and needs, and as a reserve for unforeseen expenses. Almost 19% of Romanians have used or would have liked to use their savings for vacations and personal experiences, and over 14% for home or car repairs. The financial targets for 2026 are mainly geared towards strengthening reserves and protecting personal stability, amid fears related in particular to health and income. Almost 20% of Romanians aim to save more than last year, and almost 15% want to protect their existing savings. At the same time, more than 30% point to health problems as their biggest financial fear, and 21% primarily fear losing their job.

The tbi bank survey on how Romanians manage their money in 2026 was conducted online in July this year, on a total sample of 1,223 internet users in Romania, of which over 53% are men, 68% work in the private sector, and over 31% have a net income of over RON 6,000.

World.title: Romania’s real estate investment volume falls to EUR 300 million in H1 2026 - report
World.content:
Romania’s real estate investment market recorded transactions worth approximately EUR 300 million in the first half of 2026, down from around EUR 400 million in the same period last year, according to a Colliers report. The consultancy estimates that the full-year volume could approach EUR 1 billion if several large transactions currently underway are completed.

Romania accounted for roughly 5% of the EUR 5.8 billion invested across the six largest Central and Eastern European economies: Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Romania, and Slovakia.

Regional investment increased by 7% year-on-year and exceeded both the five-year average of EUR 4.6 billion and the ten-year average of EUR 5.1 billion. Colliers expects the regional total to reach EUR 12.5-13 billion in 2026, compared with EUR 11.6 billion last year.

“The decline in transaction volumes in Romania during the period under review should be seen in a broader context,” said Robert Miklo, partner and head of capital markets at Colliers.

He noted that several deals are in progress, while the sale of a MAS retail portfolio to AFI Europe was completed shortly after the end of the reporting period, shifting the transaction into the third quarter.

“If other large transactions currently in progress are also completed, 2026 has the potential to close with investment volumes of close to EUR 1 billion, which would make it only the second year since 2007 in which the market has reached this threshold,” Miklo said.

Office properties generated approximately 60% of Romania’s transaction volume during the first half, their highest share since 2022. Colliers expects that percentage to decline as major deals in other sectors are completed during the remainder of the year.

“Influenced by the limited supply of properties available for sale, investment volumes remain below the level suggested by both investor appetite and the size of the local economy. In the first half of the year, Romania attracted just 5.4% of the investment volume recorded across the six largest economies in the region, despite accounting for almost 18% of their combined GDP. This gap shows that the local market still has substantial room for growth,” added Robert Miklo.

In Bucharest, prime yields stood at approximately 7.5% for offices, 7.75% for industrial and logistics properties, and 7.25% for shopping centers. These levels remained above those recorded in Warsaw, Prague, and Bratislava.

Colliers said investors are increasingly prioritizing assets with stable income, good energy performance, and clear long-term value prospects. Properties with weaker energy performance face tighter lending standards and lower demand.

“Financing conditions are favorable, but the advantage lies with high-quality properties with stable income, credible sponsors, and clear sustainability strategies,” Miklo said.

Across Central and Eastern Europe, Poland led the market with more than EUR 3 billion in transactions, representing 52% of the regional total. The Czech Republic followed with more than EUR 1.4 billion, while Hungary recorded close to EUR 600 million.

Offices accounted for 29% of regional investment, followed by retail at 27%, residential at 19%, and industrial and logistics assets at 17%.

World.title: Romanian animated short film selected in UK’s Official Encounters Competition
World.content:
Happy New Year, the Romanian animated short film directed by Radu Gaciu and produced by Adriana Bumbeș through Ariadna Films, has been selected for the Official Competition of the Encounters Film Festival. The film will have its world premiere on September 23, 2026, at Watershed in Bristol.

The film, set in 2009 in Romania, follows a woman who returns home on her birthday to the isolated cabin in the mountains where she spent part of her youth with her twin sister. She rediscovers a space where memory and dreams intertwine and where echoes of the past speak of the pain of separation.

With a running time of 25 minutes, Happy New Year is a fantasy drama made using a mixed 2D digital animation technique.

Encounters is a qualifying festival for the BAFTA, BIFA and European Film Awards and also gives filmmakers the chance to enter the race for the Academy Awards, in the Best Animated Short Film category. The film is eligible for the Animated Encounters Grand Prix and the Audience Award.

The movie was built over five years of work, two years of pre-production and three years of production. The animation was based on more than 60,000 reference photographs, used to build the characters and backgrounds. The project brought together a team of more than 25 people, from actresses and screenwriters to production, sound and image specialists. The film’s visual universe was created from several thousand digitally made elements, characters and backgrounds, complemented by almost 100 unique watercolor paintings.

“The film’s animation technique is mixed, a combination of digital drawing, rotoscoping and collage, in which both the characters and the settings are stylistically rendered realistically. The characters are predominantly digital drawings that were later animated or, in a few cases, rotoscoped, also digitally. The backgrounds are complex collages of adjusted photographs composed with the help of additional graphic elements,” director Radu Gaciu said.

The lead role is voiced by Ana Ularu, one of the Romanian actresses with the most solid and visible international career. The voice cast is completed by Ana-Maria Guran, Clara Angela Roman and Oana Rotaru.

The project’s journey began at the Animest International Festival, where Happy New Year won the 2020 edition of the Pitch, Please! competition. The award took the project to the CEE Animation Forum 2021. The project continued its development and production in Romania, received production support from the National Cinematography Center, and was completed on January 31, 2026.

The film is produced by Ariadna Films. The screenplay is by Radu Gaciu and Nicoleta Colopelnic, while the producer is Adriana Bumbeș.

The film’s original music was specially composed by Matei Vasilache.

World.title: President Nicușor Dan to lead Romania’s delegation to UN General Assembly
World.content:
President Nicușor Dan will lead Romania’s delegation to the high-level segment of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, which will take place in New York next month, according to an announcement from the Presidential Administration.

The central theme of the next UN session is 'Restoring trust, managing transformation: A United Nations that delivers for all.'

The head of state will deliver the national statement in the plenary session of the UN General Assembly on September 23. He will highlight Romania’s efforts to support the organization’s reform process and the country’s contribution to ensuring peace, security and an international order based on rules and norms, according to the same source.

This is the first time president Nicușor Dan will attend the UN General Assembly. Last year, Romania was represented by foreign minister Oana Țoiu. Dan explained at the time that he did not go to New York because he considered it “more useful” to be present in the country.

At the next UN assembly, the president will also participate in New York in events organized on the sidelines of the high-level segment. He will hold bilateral meetings with other heads of state or government, including to support Romania’s candidacy for the leadership of the International Organisation of La Francophonie.

Former European Commissioner Dacian Cioloș is supported by Romania for the position of Secretary General of the OIF.

World.title: Environment Ministry says Romania exceeded PNRR target with over 5,000 recycling islands completed
World.content:
Romania has completed 5,091 digitized recycling islands nationwide, exceeding its target of 5,000 under the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR), the Environment Ministry announced. The investment’s total budget is EUR 72.75 million.

The waste collection systems have been installed across 36 counties, with Bacău, Bihor, Arad, Cluj, and Constanța among those hosting the largest numbers.

“The commissioning of these thousands of islands contributes to modernizing Romania’s waste management infrastructure,” interim environment minister Diana Buzoianu said. “Through the National Recovery and Resilience Plan, we managed to exceed the target of 5,000 islands and help Romanians make the transition to a circular economy more easily.”

The systems allow waste to be separated into five categories: paper and cardboard, plastic and metal, glass, biodegradable waste, and residual waste.

“Beyond projects and financing, the circular economy is built through cooperation between authorities, the private sector, and citizens,” minister Buzoianu also said. “These islands will contribute to a cleaner environment in the communities where they operate.”

Three types of collection systems were financed through the program: enclosed above-ground islands, above-ground islands with individual containers, and underground islands with individual containers. According to the ministry, the underground systems are intended in part for urban and tourist areas where available space is limited.

The investment also includes the development of a software platform for operating the recycling islands and managing the data they generate. It further covers measures to promote the “pay-as-you-throw” principle.

World.title: Animation film festival Animest returns to Bucharest in October with nature-themed edition
World.content:
The Animest International Animation Film Festival will hold its 21st edition in Bucharest from October 2 to 11, with a program exploring the relationship between people and the natural environment. Screenings and events will take place at Cinema Muzeul Țăranului, Cinemateca Eforie, Instituto Cervantes, and CINETic.

The thematic section will comprise three short-film programs titled Living with Nature, Human Nature, and Nature, curated by Animest artistic director Mihai Mitrică and French film journalist and historian Alexis Hunot.

“We propose three directions for observing how animated film approaches vital topics: questioning our relationship with the environment, reflecting on human nature, and imagining nature in our absence,” Hunot said.

The selection includes Karni Arieli and Saul Freed’s Wild Summon, which presents the life cycle of wild salmon through human figures, and Mark Baker’s The Village, a black comedy about the inhabitants of an isolated community. Other titles include Chris Landreth’s Ryan, which explores the life of Canadian animator Ryan Larkin, and Vergine Keaton’s Je criais contre la vie. Ou pour elle, in which a herd of deer begins hunting the dogs that pursued it.

The festival’s 2026 visual identity was created by Brazilian-Welsh illustrator and animation director Luiz Stockler. It depicts nature entering an urban apartment and transforming the interior into a plant-filled space.

Animest is also accepting applications for two programs aimed at Romanian animation creators. TOON SCRIPTS is a competition for animated series concepts and scripts, while PITCH, PLEASE! is a development workshop for animated short-film projects. Applications for both programs remain open until September 7 through the festival’s official website.

World.title: Romanian startup launches tool to assess websites’ visibility in AI search
World.content:
Romanian company Human AI Labs has launched Blind Spot, a platform that assesses whether websites can be understood, cited, and recommended by generative AI systems. The tool evaluates sites against 70 technical and content-related criteria and generates an AI visibility score.

Blind Spot analyzes factors including access for AI crawlers, structured data, semantic clarity, quotable content, digital authority, and trust signals. It then identifies issues that could make a website difficult for generative systems to interpret or cite and provides recommendations for addressing them.

The platform is designed for services such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude, and Google AI Overviews, which can extract and synthesize information rather than only display lists of links.

“For years, companies optimized for Google: keywords, backlinks, titles, and meta tags. All of these remain important, but AI search works differently,” said Human AI Labs founder Andrei Mihnea Răileanu. “It needs structure, clarity, coherent data, easily quotable content, and authority signals that it can verify. A website can be excellent for people and still be difficult for AI to read.”

Unlike tools that monitor how brands appear in AI-generated answers, Blind Spot focuses on a website’s underlying infrastructure. Its score is calculated using deterministic criteria without AI participating in the evaluation, according to the company. For some technical issues, the generated report can also include code examples or implementation guidance.

During its beta stage, Blind Spot audited several Romanian websites and recorded an average AI visibility score of 48 out of 100. The most common issues included incomplete structured data, content that was difficult to cite, unclear authority signals, and an inconsistent presence in sources that AI systems could treat as references.

Human AI Labs filed a patent application with Romania’s State Office for Inventions and Trademarks (OSIM) in June 2026 covering elements of the platform’s architecture, including its normalized extraction methodology, deterministic scoring, and semantic gap analysis.

Blind Spot is available online, with a free audit covering the first pages of a website. The platform also offers six months of free access to eligible nongovernmental organizations and a free diagnostic audit for startups.

World.title: Western Romania: Thick smoke covers city of Timişoara for second day as wildfires rage in Serbia
World.content:
A thick layer of smoke covered Timişoara on Friday, August 21, for the second consecutive day, following recent out-of-control wildfires in Serbia. In response, authorities recommended that residents stay indoors.

Thousands of hectares of forests and grassland have burned in the neighboring country in recent days, and smoke easily crossed into Romania. A day earlier, on Thursday, August 20, dozens of calls to the 112 emergency number from Timişoara and the county reported a strong smell of smoke, according to News.ro.

Sent to verify the surroundings, Romanian firefighters said that no fires were identified. “Based on the information available, the smoke observed in Timiş County could most likely originate from the large-scale dry vegetation fires in the Dubovac area, Serbia. Depending on weather conditions and wind direction, the smoke may also be felt in our county,” ISU Timiş said.

In recent days, no fewer than 45 vegetation fires have been recorded, with the most intense one in the sandy Deliblato area of Serbia, a nature reserve in the northeast of the country, where flames have burned approximately 3,500 hectares of vegetation.

Two other major active fires are in the Stolovi mountain area (Serbia), where approximately 200 hectares of forest and low vegetation have burned, and further south of it, where around 60 hectares of forest have burned.

Serbia has appealed to Russia for help in fighting forest fires due to the lack of aircraft available from the European Union, the country’s Interior Ministry announced. Serbia is not an EU member, but has access to EU emergency assistance through the European bloc’s Civil Protection Mechanism. This summer, Belgrade sent a firefighting helicopter and an emergency response team to help Spain fight forest fires under this mechanism, but forest fires across Europe have depleted EU resources.

Until the fires are extinguished, the Timiş Public Health Directorate recommended that the population close their windows and refrain from outdoor activities. “This situation may lead to an aggravation of respiratory symptoms, especially among vulnerable people with chronic respiratory conditions (bronchial asthma, etc.) and cardiovascular conditions,” DSP Timiş said.

Lead consultant in pulmonology in Timişoara, Cristian Oancea, provided further recommendations, noting that smoke from vegetation fires contains a mixture of fine particles and toxic gases that can affect the respiratory system, including in healthy people.

“One of the main dangers is represented by fine PM2.5 particles. Due to their very small size, they can penetrate deep into the respiratory tract and reach the level of the pulmonary alveoli. Even short-term exposure to high concentrations of smoke can irritate the eyes, nose and throat, cause coughing, runny nose, wheezing, a feeling of pressure in the chest or shortness of breath,” he said on Facebook.

Moreover, according to the doctor, smoke produced by fires can also contain carbon monoxide, a toxic gas that, at high concentrations, prevents the normal transport of oxygen in the body. “For people diagnosed with asthma, COPD, bronchiectasis, emphysema, pulmonary fibrosis or other chronic respiratory diseases, exposure to smoke can lead to worsening symptoms or the occurrence of an exacerbation. In severe cases, going to the emergency room or even hospitalization may be necessary,” he added.

Timiş County Council vice-president Alexandru Iovescu commented on the situation and said that Serbia has not yet requested the help of firefighters from Timiş County to extinguish the vegetation fires.

The official noted that the Environmental Guard has activated the sensors for monitoring air quality. “There is no reason to panic, but it is good to be careful and follow the recommendations of specialists. We are in contact with the responsible institutions and will communicate any important information,” Iovescu said.
